# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/wechat_group.jpg](Figure/wechat_group.jpg)
- [README.md](README.md)
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py)

</details>



SaprotHub is a framework designed to democratize protein language model (PLM) training and usage for biologists without requiring extensive machine learning expertise. It provides user-friendly interfaces and tools that enable researchers to train, fine-tune, share, and collaborate on protein language models for various biological prediction tasks.

For more detailed information about specific concepts introduced here, see [Key Concepts and Terminology](#1.1).

## System Architecture

SaprotHub integrates several components that work together to provide a seamless experience for biologists working with protein language models.

### High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    User["Biologist/Researcher"] --> |"Interacts with"| Colab["Google Colab"]
    User --> |"or"| LocalServer["Local Server"]
    
    Colab --> |"Runs"| ColabSaprot["ColabSaprot Interface"]
    LocalServer --> |"Runs"| ColabSaprot
    
    subgraph "Interfaces"
        ColabSaprot --> |"Primary"| SaprotNotebook["SaprotHub Notebook"]
        ColabSaprot --> |"Specialized"| ColabProtT5["ColabProtT5"]
        ColabSaprot --> |"Specialized"| ColabProTrek["ColabProTrek"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Training"
        SaprotNotebook --> TrainPipeline["Training Pipeline"]
        
        TrainPipeline --> |"Utilizes"| PLM["Protein Language Models"]
        TrainPipeline --> |"Uses"| PEFT["Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning"]
        TrainPipeline --> |"Creates"| Adapters["Task-specific Adapters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Flow"
        SaprotNotebook --> DataInput["Data Input Methods"]
        DataInput --> |"Process"| LMDB["LMDB Datasets"]
        LMDB --> TrainingPipeline["Training Pipeline"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Sharing"
        Adapters --> HFHub["HuggingFace Hub"]
        HFHub --> |"Download models"| SaprotNotebook
    end
```

Sources:
- [README.md:1-10]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:1-37]()

## Core Components

### ColabSaprot Interface

The ColabSaprot interface is the primary way researchers interact with SaprotHub. It provides a user-friendly environment in Google Colab or local servers for protein language model tasks.

#### Supported Input Types

| Input Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Single AA Sequence | Amino acid sequence input |
| Single SA Sequence | Structure-aware sequence input |
| Single UniProt ID | UniProt database identifier |
| Single PDB/CIF Structure | 3D protein structure file |
| Multiple AA/SA Sequences | Batch processing of sequences |
| Pair Sequences | For protein-protein interaction tasks |
| SaprotHub Dataset | Pre-processed datasets from the hub |

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:45-60]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:250-329]()

### Model Architecture

SaprotHub implements a hierarchical model structure organized by task type:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    AbstractModel <|-- SaprotBaseModel
    AbstractModel <|-- ProtT5BaseModel
    
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotRegressionModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotTokenClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairRegressionModel
    
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5ClassificationModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5RegressionModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5TokenClassificationModel
    
    class AbstractModel {
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +test_step()
    }
    
    class SaprotBaseModel {
        +task: str
        +config_path: str
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
        +get_hidden_states_from_seqs()
    }
    
    class ProtT5BaseModel {
        +task: str
        +config_path: str
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
    }
```

The task types in SaprotHub's model hierarchy include:

| Task Type | Model Suffix | Description |
|-----------|--------------|-------------|
| `classification` | `SaprotClassificationModel` | Protein-level classification tasks (e.g., function prediction) |
| `regression` | `SaprotRegressionModel` | Protein-level regression tasks (e.g., stability prediction) |
| `token_classification` | `SaprotTokenClassificationModel` | Residue-level classification tasks (e.g., secondary structure) |
| `pair_classification` | `SaprotPairClassificationModel` | Protein-protein interaction classification |
| `pair_regression` | `SaprotPairRegressionModel` | Protein-protein interaction regression |

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:290-311]()

### Data Processing Pipeline

The data processing pipeline is responsible for converting various input formats into structured datasets for model training.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["User Input Data"] --> DataType{"Data Type?"}
    
    DataType -->|"AA Sequence"| AASeq["Amino Acid Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"SA Sequence"| SASeq["Structure-Aware Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"UniProt ID"| UniProt["UniProt Identifier"]
    DataType -->|"PDB/CIF Structure"| PDBStruct["Protein Structure"]
    DataType -->|"Multiple Sequences"| MultiSeq["Multiple Sequences CSV"]
    DataType -->|"Multiple Structures"| MultiStruct["Multiple Structures CSV"]
    
    AASeq --> Process["Data Processing"]
    SASeq --> Process
    UniProt --> |"Download Structure"| AlphaFold["AlphaFold DB"]
    AlphaFold --> Process
    PDBStruct --> |"Extract Chain"| Process
    MultiSeq --> Process
    MultiStruct --> Process
    
    Process --> |"Structure Extraction"| Foldseek["Foldseek Utility"]
    Process --> Tokenization["Sequence Tokenization"]
    
    Foldseek --> SAConversion["Convert to SA Sequence"]
    Tokenization --> Encoding["Model Encoding"]
    SAConversion --> Encoding
    
    Encoding --> LMDB["LMDB Database"]
    LMDB --> TrainingPipeline["Training Pipeline"]
```

Key steps in the data processing pipeline:

1. **Input Processing**: Handles various data formats including AA sequences, SA sequences, UniProt IDs, and PDB/CIF files
2. **Structure Extraction**: Uses Foldseek to extract structural information from 3D protein structures
3. **Data Conversion**: Transforms inputs into formats suitable for model training
4. **LMDB Storage**: Stores processed data in LMDB format for efficient access during training

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:574-627]()
- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:12-87]()

### Training Pipeline with LoRA

SaprotHub uses Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for efficient fine-tuning of protein language models.

```mermaid
graph TB
    PretrainedModel["Pre-trained Protein Language Model"] --> ModelChoice{"Model Type"}
    ModelChoice -->|"SaProt"| SaprotBaseModel["SaProt Base Model"]
    ModelChoice -->|"ProtT5"| ProtT5Model["ProtT5 Base Model"]
    
    SaprotBaseModel --> LoRA["LoRA Adapter Integration"]
    ProtT5Model --> LoRA
    
    LoRA --> TaskAdapter{"Task-specific Adapter"}
    TaskAdapter -->|"Classification"| ClsAdapter["Classification Adapter"]
    TaskAdapter -->|"Regression"| RegAdapter["Regression Adapter"]
    TaskAdapter -->|"Token Classification"| TokenAdapter["Token Classification Adapter"]
    TaskAdapter -->|"Pair Tasks"| PairAdapter["Pair Tasks Adapter"]
    
    ClsAdapter --> FinetuneProcess["Fine-tuning Process"]
    RegAdapter --> FinetuneProcess
    TokenAdapter --> FinetuneProcess
    PairAdapter --> FinetuneProcess
    
    FinetuneProcess --> SaveAdapter["Save Adapter"]
    SaveAdapter --> |"Upload"| HuggingFace["HuggingFace Hub"]
    SaveAdapter --> |"Local Storage"| LocalAdapter["Local Adapter"]
    
    HuggingFace --> |"Download for inference"| Inference["Model Inference"]
    LocalAdapter --> Inference
```

The LoRA approach offers several advantages:

1. **Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning**: Only trains a small number of parameters rather than the entire model
2. **Reduced Memory Requirements**: Enables training on hardware with limited resources
3. **Easy Sharing**: Small adapter files (typically <10MB) instead of full models
4. **Flexible Deployment**: Adapters can be swapped without reloading the base model

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:347-456]()

## Deployment Options

SaprotHub can be deployed in two main environments:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    User["Researcher/Biologist"] --> DeployChoice{"Deployment Choice"}
    
    DeployChoice -->|"Cloud Option"| Colab["Google Colab"]
    DeployChoice -->|"Local Option"| LocalServer["Local Server"]
    
    subgraph "Google Colab Deployment"
        Colab --> |"Open"| SaprotNotebook["SaprotHub.ipynb"]
        SaprotNotebook --> |"Select"| GPUType["GPU Type: T4/L4/A100"]
        SaprotNotebook --> |"Run"| Installation["Install Dependencies"]
        Installation --> ColabRun["Run SaprotHub"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Local Server Deployment"
        LocalServer --> |"OS Type?"| OSChoice{"OS Type"}
        OSChoice -->|"Linux"| LinuxSetup["bash install.sh"]
        OSChoice -->|"Windows"| WindowsSetup["Docker Deployment"]
        
        LinuxSetup --> RunServer["bash run.sh"]
        WindowsSetup --> RunServer
        
        RunServer --> JupyterServer["Jupyter Server"]
        JupyterServer --> |"Connect"| ColabInterface["Colab Interface"]
        JupyterServer --> |"Port 12315"| Token["Token: SaprotHub"]
    end
    
    ColabRun --> ModelTraining["Model Training/Prediction"]
    ColabInterface --> ModelTraining
```

### Google Colab Deployment

The Google Colab deployment is the simplest option for most users:

1. Open the SaprotHub notebook in Google Colab
2. Select an appropriate GPU type based on your needs:
   - T4 GPU (Free): For basic tasks and smaller models
   - L4 GPU (Colab Pro): For larger models with more memory
   - A100 GPU (Colab Pro): For training large models with highest performance
3. Run the installation cell
4. Use the interactive interface

### Local Server Deployment

For those who prefer local deployment or need more control:

1. Clone the SaprotHub repository
2. Install dependencies using the provided scripts:
   - Linux: Use `install.sh` and `run.sh`
   - Windows: Deploy through Docker
3. Access the Jupyter server on port 12315 with token "SaprotHub"
4. Connect to the ColabSaprot interface

Sources:
- [README.md:26-27]()
- [local_server/jupyter_notebook_config.py:930-939]()
- [colab/not_use_only_for_dev.ipynb:41-49]()

## Community Model Sharing

SaprotHub facilitates community collaboration through the Open Protein Modeling Consortium (OPMC), a collaborative initiative aimed at democratizing protein language models.

Key features of the community sharing approach:

1. **HuggingFace Integration**: Models trained in SaprotHub can be directly uploaded to HuggingFace
2. **Adapter-Based Sharing**: Small, task-specific adapters instead of full models
3. **Cross-Institution Collaboration**: Researchers from different institutions can build on each other's models
4. **Specialized Interfaces**: Support for multiple protein language models through specialized interfaces

The OPMC currently includes several tools:
- ColabSaprot (AA+3Di sequences)
- ColabProTrek (sequence-structure alignment)
- ColabProtT5 (amino acid sequences)
- ColabMETL (mutational effect transfer learning)
- Other specialized protein modeling tools (Evolla, Pinal, ProTrek)

Sources:
- [README.md:30-43]()
- [README.md:175-178]()

## Summary

SaprotHub provides a comprehensive framework for democratizing protein language models through:

1. **User-Friendly Interfaces**: Making sophisticated models accessible to biologists
2. **Efficient Fine-Tuning**: Using LoRA to enable training on limited resources
3. **Flexible Data Processing**: Supporting various protein data formats
4. **Collaborative Ecosystem**: Facilitating model sharing and collaboration
5. **Multiple Deployment Options**: Supporting both cloud and local deployment

For more details on specific components, see the related pages on the [ColabSaprot Interface](#2), [Model Architecture](#3), [Data Processing](#4), [Training Pipeline](#5), and [Deployment Options](#6).

This page introduces the fundamental concepts and terminology used throughout the SaprotHub ecosystem. It covers protein language models, key data structures, model architecture, and common workflows that form the foundation of the SaprotHub platform. For specific details on interfaces and usage, see [ColabSaprot Interface](#2).

## 1. Protein Language Models

Protein Language Models (PLMs) are a class of machine learning models that learn the statistical patterns in protein sequences, similar to how language models learn patterns in text. In SaprotHub, PLMs serve as the foundation for various protein analysis tasks.

### 1.1 SaProt Framework

SaProt is the underlying protein language model framework in SaprotHub. It's designed to process both amino acid sequences and structural information about proteins.

Key characteristics of SaProt:
- Pre-trained on diverse protein datasets
- Available in different model sizes (35M, 650M parameters)
- Designed to support both sequence-based and structure-aware analysis

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Protein Language Models"
        PLM["PLM Core Functionality"] --> SaProt["SaProt Models"]
        PLM --> ProtT5["ProtT5 Models"]
        
        SaProt --> SapSmall["SaProt-35M"]
        SaProt --> SapLarge["SaProt-650M"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Input Types"
        AA["Amino Acid Sequences (AA)"]
        SA["Structure-Aware Sequences (SA)"]
    end
    
    AA --> PLM
    SA --> PLM
    
    subgraph "Task Types"
        PLM --> Classification["Protein Classification"]
        PLM --> TokenClassification["Residue-level Classification"]
        PLM --> Regression["Protein Regression"]
        PLM --> PairClass["Protein-Protein Classification"]
        PLM --> PairReg["Protein-Protein Regression"]
    end
```

Sources: [README.md:20-27](README.md), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:19-25](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

### 1.2 Types of Protein Sequences

SaprotHub works with two primary types of protein sequence data:

1. **Amino Acid (AA) Sequences**: The traditional representation of proteins as chains of amino acids, using the standard 20-letter alphabet (A, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, K, L, M, N, P, Q, R, S, T, V, W, Y).

2. **Structure-Aware (SA) Sequences**: Enhanced protein representations that incorporate 3D structural information alongside the amino acid sequence. These are typically derived from PDB files or AlphaFold predictions using tools like Foldseek.

**Example:**
- AA sequence: `MKKLILVLLFVGAFNACQGTDNSKVCTASQDPYSAALQGCTIEWAK`
- SA sequence: Combines amino acid and structural tokens in alternating pattern

Sources: [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:11-87](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:251-251](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

## 2. Model Architecture

SaprotHub employs a hierarchical model architecture that enables different types of protein analysis tasks.

### 2.1 Model Hierarchy

```mermaid
classDiagram
    AbstractModel <|-- SaprotBaseModel
    AbstractModel <|-- ProtT5BaseModel
    
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotRegressionModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotTokenClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairRegressionModel
    
    class AbstractModel {
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +test_step()
    }
    
    class SaprotBaseModel {
        +task: str
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
        +get_hidden_states_from_seqs()
        +_init_lora()
    }
    
    class SaprotClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +predict()
    }
    
    class SaprotRegressionModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +predict()
    }
    
    class SaprotTokenClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +predict()
    }
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:295-303](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

### 2.2 Task-Specific Models

SaprotHub supports five main types of models for different protein analysis tasks:

| Model Type | Task Type | Description | Example Use Cases |
|------------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| Classification | `classification` | Predicts discrete protein-level labels | Protein function prediction, subcellular localization |
| Regression | `regression` | Predicts continuous protein-level values | Thermostability, solubility prediction |
| Token Classification | `token_classification` | Predicts properties for each amino acid residue | Secondary structure prediction, binding site identification |
| Pair Classification | `pair_classification` | Predicts binary relationships between protein pairs | Protein-protein interaction prediction |
| Pair Regression | `pair_regression` | Predicts continuous values for protein pairs | Binding affinity prediction |

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:290-326](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

## 3. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

SaprotHub uses Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) techniques to make it feasible to adapt large protein language models to specific tasks without requiring excessive computational resources.

### 3.1 LoRA Adapters

Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the primary PEFT method used in SaprotHub. Instead of fine-tuning all parameters of a large model, LoRA adds small trainable "adapter" modules to selected layers of the frozen pre-trained model.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Pre-trained Model"
        PretrainedParams["Frozen Parameters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "LoRA Components"
        LoRADown["Low-Rank Downprojection"]
        LoRAUp["Low-Rank Upprojection"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task-Specific Components"
        TaskAdapter["Task-specific Adapter"]
        TaskHead["Task-specific Prediction Head"]
    end
    
    Input["Protein Sequence Input"] --> PretrainedParams
    PretrainedParams --> LoRADown
    LoRADown --> LoRAUp
    LoRAUp --> TaskAdapter
    TaskAdapter --> TaskHead
    TaskHead --> Output["Prediction Output"]
    
    PretrainedParams -.- |"+ Small delta"|LoRAUp
```

Key benefits of LoRA in SaprotHub:
- Reduces the number of trainable parameters (typically <1% of the full model)
- Decreases memory requirements and allows training on standard GPUs
- Enables sharing of lightweight adapters (~1MB) instead of full models (~2GB)
- Facilitates community collaboration through adapter sharing

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:362-431](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb), [README.md:30-33](README.md)

### 4.2 Data Processing Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["User Input Data"] --> DataType{Data Type?}
    
    DataType -->|AA Sequence| AASeq[Amino Acid Sequence]
    DataType -->|SA Sequence| SASeq[Structure-Aware Sequence]
    DataType -->|UniProt ID| UniProt[UniProt Identifier]
    DataType -->|PDB/CIF Structure| PDBStruct[Protein Structure]
    
    UniProt --> |Download Structure| AlphaFold[AlphaFold DB]
    AlphaFold --> PDBStruct
    
    PDBStruct --> |Extract Chain| Process[Extract Chain]
    Process --> |Extract Structure| Foldseek[Foldseek Conversion]
    
    Foldseek --> SAConversion[Convert to SA Sequence]
    AASeq --> Tokenization[Sequence Tokenization]
    SAConversion --> Tokenization
    
    Tokenization --> Encoding[Model Encoding]
    
    Encoding --> LMDB[(LMDB Database)]
    LMDB --> TrainingPipeline[Training Pipeline]
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:11-87](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:522-567](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

## 5. Training and Prediction Workflows

SaprotHub supports several key workflows for training models and making predictions:

### 5.1 Training Workflow

The training process in SaprotHub typically involves:

1. **Data preparation**: Converting input data to LMDB format
2. **Model selection**: Choosing the appropriate base model and task
3. **Adapter configuration**: Setting up LoRA parameters
4. **Training**: Fine-tuning the adapter for the specific task
5. **Evaluation**: Assessing model performance on validation data
6. **Adapter sharing**: Optionally sharing the adapter on SaprotHub

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "Biologist/Researcher"
    participant Interface as "ColabSaprot Interface"
    participant Data as "Data Processor"
    participant Model as "SaProt Model"
    participant Adapter as "LoRA Adapter"
    participant HF as "HuggingFace Hub"
    
    User->>Interface: Input data & select task
    Interface->>Data: Prepare data
    Data->>Data: Convert to LMDB
    Interface->>Model: Initialize frozen pre-trained model
    Interface->>Adapter: Initialize task-specific adapter
    Interface->>Model: Train with adapter
    Model->>Interface: Return performance metrics
    Interface->>User: Display results
    opt Share Adapter
        User->>Interface: Request to share adapter
        Interface->>HF: Upload adapter to SaprotHub
        HF->>Interface: Confirm upload
        Interface->>User: Share adapter URL
    end
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:400-456](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

### 5.2 Prediction Workflows

SaprotHub supports several prediction workflows:

1. **Standard Prediction**: Use a trained model to predict properties of new proteins
2. **Mutational Effect Prediction**: Assess the impact of mutations on protein properties
3. **Inverse Folding Prediction**: Design sequences based on target structures

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:46-54](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

## 6. Deployment Options

### 6.1 Google Colab (ColabSaprot)

The primary interface for SaprotHub is ColabSaprot, which runs in Google Colab notebooks. This allows users to access SaprotHub without local installation requirements.

Key features:
- Free access with T4 GPUs (basic tasks)
- Higher-tier GPUs available with Colab Pro (L4, A100)
- Interactive interface for data input, model training, and prediction
- Easy sharing of models through HuggingFace Hub

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:41-53](colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)

### 6.2 Local Server Deployment

For users who need more computational resources or persistent environments, SaprotHub can be deployed on local servers.

Key features:
- Support for Linux and Windows (via Docker)
- Custom installation scripts for dependencies
- Access through Jupyter Server interface
- Persistent storage of models and data

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Local Server Deployment"
        LocalServer[Local Server] --> |OS Type?| OSChoice{OS Type}
        OSChoice -->|Linux| LinuxSetup[bash install.sh]
        OSChoice -->|Windows| WindowsSetup[Docker Deployment]
        
        LinuxSetup --> RunServer[bash run.sh]
        WindowsSetup --> RunServer
        
        RunServer --> JupyterServer[Jupyter Server]
        JupyterServer --> |Connect| LocalInterface[Web Interface]
        JupyterServer --> |Port 12315| Token[Token: SaprotHub]
    end
    
    LocalInterface --> ModelTraining[Model Training/Prediction]
```

Sources: [README.md:26-27](README.md), [local_server/jupyter_notebook_config.py:1-30](local_server/jupyter_notebook_config.py)

## 7. SaprotHub Community and Ecosystem

SaprotHub is part of the Open Protein Modeling Consortium (OPMC), which aims to democratize protein language models for the biology community.

Key components of the ecosystem:
- **SaprotHub**: Central repository for model sharing
- **ColabSaprot**: User interface for SaProt models
- **ColabProtT5**: Interface for ProtT5 models
- **ColabProTrek**: Interface for ProTrek models
- **Additional OPMC tools**: Including METL, Evolla, Pinal, and others

Sources: [README.md:29-43](README.md)

## 8. Terminology Reference

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| PLM | Protein Language Model - Machine learning model trained to understand protein sequences |
| AA Sequence | Amino Acid Sequence - Standard one-letter code representation of proteins |
| SA Sequence | Structure-Aware Sequence - Enhanced representation that includes structural information |
| LoRA | Low-Rank Adaptation - Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method |
| PEFT | Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning - Techniques to adapt models with minimal parameters |
| Adapter | Small, trainable module that modifies a pre-trained model's behavior |
| LMDB | Lightning Memory-Mapped Database - High-performance database used for storing protein data |
| OPMC | Open Protein Modeling Consortium - Collaborative initiative for protein modeling |
| ColabSaprot | Google Colab interface for SaProt models |
| SaprotHub | Repository and community platform for sharing protein models |

Sources: [README.md:8-43](README.md), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:19-37](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)

# Page: ColabSaprot Interface

# ColabSaprot Interface

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/training_curve_cls.png](Figure/training_curve_cls.png)
- [Figure/training_curve_reg.png](Figure/training_curve_reg.png)
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)
- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py)

</details>



## Overview

The ColabSaprot Interface is the primary user-facing component of SaprotHub, designed to democratize access to protein language models (PLMs) for biologists with limited machine learning expertise. This interface runs in Google Colab, providing a notebook-based environment where users can easily input protein data, train models, make predictions, and share trained models with the scientific community.

ColabSaprot specifically focuses on making the [SaProt](https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProt) protein language model accessible through a user-friendly interface, eliminating the need for coding expertise or specialized hardware while maintaining robust functionality for protein modeling tasks.

For information about model architecture specifics, see [Model Architecture](#3). For details on data processing, see [Data Processing](#4).

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:9-37]()
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:6-27]()

## Architecture and Components

ColabSaprot is structured as a Jupyter notebook interface that connects users to the SaProt model ecosystem. It serves as an abstraction layer that simplifies the complexity of protein language models by providing intuitive workflows for various protein prediction tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "ColabSaprot Interface"
        Inst[Installation Section] --> Input[Data Input Methods]
        Input --> ModelSel[Model Selection]
        ModelSel --> Training[Model Training]
        Training --> Prediction[Prediction Functions]
        Prediction --> ModelSharing[Model Sharing]
    end

    subgraph "Backend Systems"
        SaprotLib["SaProt Library"] <--> Models["Protein Language Models"]
        SaprotLib <--> HFHub["HuggingFace Hub"]
        SaprotLib <--> Foldseek["Foldseek Utility"]
        SaprotLib <--> LMDB["LMDB Storage"]
    end

    Input <--> SaprotLib
    ModelSel <--> SaprotLib
    Training <--> SaprotLib
    Prediction <--> SaprotLib
    ModelSharing <--> HFHub

    subgraph "User Interaction"
        User["Biologist User"] --> |"Runs"| ColabSaprot["ColabSaprot Notebook"]
        ColabSaprot --> |"Interfaces with"| Inst
    end
    
    classDef interface fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    classDef backend fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    class "ColabSaprot Interface" interface
    class "Backend Systems" backend
```

**Key Interface Components:**

| Component | Purpose | Functions |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| Installation Section | Set up the environment | Install dependencies, check GPU status |
| Data Input Methods | Provide various ways to input protein data | Accept sequences, structures, IDs |
| Model Selection | Choose from available models | Browse local and shared models |
| Model Training | Configure and train models | Set hyperparameters, execute training |
| Prediction Functions | Apply models to make predictions | Classification, regression, mutational effects |
| Model Sharing | Share trained models with the community | Upload to HuggingFace Hub |

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:46-59]()
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:37-59]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:81-99]()

## Data Flow in ColabSaprot

ColabSaprot has a structured data flow that processes various protein data inputs and transforms them for model training and inference:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Methods"
        AASeq["Single AA Sequence"]
        SASeq["Single SA Sequence"]
        UniProt["UniProt ID"]
        PDBStruct["PDB/CIF Structure"]
        MultiSeq["Multiple Sequences CSV"]
        MultiStruct["Multiple Structures CSV+ZIP"]
        PairSeq["Sequence Pairs"]
    end

    subgraph "Data Processing"
        Parser["Data Type Parser"]
        AASeq --> Parser
        SASeq --> Parser
        UniProt --> Parser
        PDBStruct --> Parser
        MultiSeq --> Parser
        MultiStruct --> Parser
        PairSeq --> Parser
        
        Parser --> DataTypeDetection["data_type_list Detection"]
        DataTypeDetection --> DataFormatter["Format for Model Input"]
    end

    subgraph "Structure Processing"
        PDBParser["PDB/CIF Parsing"]
        FoldseekConversion["get_struc_seq Function"]
        PLDDTFiltering["plddt_mask Filtering"]
        
        PDBStruct --> PDBParser
        MultiStruct --> PDBParser
        PDBParser --> FoldseekConversion
        FoldseekConversion --> PLDDTFiltering
        PLDDTFiltering --> |"Returns SA Sequences"| DataFormatter
    end

    subgraph "Model Interface"
        DataFormatter --> LMDBCreation["LMDB Dataset Creation"]
        LMDBCreation --> ModelInput["Model Training/Inference"]
    end

    classDef processing fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px
    class "Data Processing" processing
    class "Structure Processing" processing
```

**Data Type Support:**
ColabSaprot supports various input data types for flexibility:

1. **Sequences**:
   - Single AA (amino acid) sequences
   - Single SA (structure-aware) sequences
   - Multiple sequences via CSV files

2. **Structures**:
   - PDB/CIF structure files
   - Multiple structure files via ZIP archives

3. **Identifiers**:
   - UniProt IDs (automatically retrieves structures)
   - SaprotHub Dataset IDs

4. **Paired Data**:
   - Sequence pairs for interaction tasks
   - Structure pairs for structural comparison

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:252-268]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:576-714]()
- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:12-87]()

## User Interface Flow

The ColabSaprot interface guides users through a sequential process for working with protein data:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as "Biologist User"
    participant Colab as "ColabSaprot Interface"
    participant Backend as "SaProt Backend"
    participant HF as "HuggingFace Hub"
    
    User->>Colab: Run Installation Cell
    Colab->>Backend: Install SaProt and Dependencies
    Backend-->>Colab: Setup Complete
    
    User->>Colab: Choose Task Type (Classification/Regression)
    User->>Colab: Select Data Input Method
    User->>Colab: Upload/Enter Protein Data
    
    Colab->>Backend: Process Input Data
    Backend->>Backend: Convert to Model Format
    Backend-->>Colab: Data Ready for Model
    
    User->>Colab: Select Model Source
    alt Use Existing Model
        User->>Colab: Enter Model ID
        Colab->>HF: Request Model
        HF-->>Colab: Download Model
    else Train New Model
        User->>Colab: Set Training Parameters
        Colab->>Backend: Train Model
        Backend-->>Colab: Training Complete
    end
    
    User->>Colab: Run Prediction
    Colab->>Backend: Execute Model Inference
    Backend-->>Colab: Return Predictions
    Colab-->>User: Display Results
    
    opt Share Model
        User->>Colab: Initiate Model Sharing
        Colab->>HF: Upload Model to SaprotHub
        HF-->>User: Model Published
    end
```

This diagram illustrates the typical user journey from installation to prediction and optional model sharing.

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:111-352]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:347-409]()

## Key Interface Features

### Installation and Setup

The installation section handles the initial setup required to use ColabSaprot:

1. **GPU Runtime Check**: Ensures the notebook is running with GPU acceleration
2. **SaProt Installation**: Installs the SaProt library and its dependencies
3. **Directory Structure Setup**: Creates the necessary directories for datasets, models, and outputs
4. **Binary Tools Setup**: Sets up the Foldseek binary for structure processing

The interface displays clear warnings about runtime limits and idle timeout policies to help users plan their usage.

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:81-99]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:111-193]()

### Data Input Methods

ColabSaprot provides multiple ways to input protein data, implementing a flexible approach to accommodate various user needs:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "input_raw_data_by_data_type Function"
        InputFunc["input_raw_data_by_data_type"]
        CheckType["Detect Data Type"]
        
        InputFunc --> CheckType
        CheckType --> |"Single Sequences"| TextInput["ipywidgets.Text Input"]
        CheckType --> |"Structure File"| StructInput["Upload + Chain Selection"]
        CheckType --> |"Multiple Sequences"| CSVInput["CSV File Upload"]
        CheckType --> |"Multiple Structures"| ZipInput["CSV + ZIP Upload"]
        CheckType --> |"SaprotHub Dataset"| IDInput["Dataset ID Input"]
        CheckType --> |"Sequence Pairs"| PairInput["Dual Sequence Input"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Type Detection"
        DetectType["get_data_type Function"]
        CheckCSV["read_csv_dataset"]
        CheckToken["Check Second Token"]
        SADetect["SA Sequence Detection"]
        AADetect["AA Sequence Detection"]
        
        DetectType --> CheckCSV
        CheckCSV --> CheckToken
        CheckToken --> |"In foldseek_struc_vocab"| SADetect
        CheckToken --> |"In aa_set"| AADetect
    end
    
    InputFunc --> DetectType
```

These input methods allow users to easily provide their protein data regardless of its format or source.

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:586-714]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:551-577]()

### Model Selection and Training

The model selection and training section allows users to:

1. **Select Model Source**:
   - Use existing models from SaprotHub
   - Train new models from scratch
   - Load models from local storage

2. **Configure Training Parameters**:
   - Model size selection (35M, 650M)
   - Batch size adjustment
   - Learning rate configuration
   - Number of training epochs

3. **Task Type Selection**:
   - Protein-level classification/regression
   - Residue-level (token) classification
   - Protein-protein classification/regression

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:347-409]()
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:290-309]()

### Model Sharing

ColabSaprot facilitates community collaboration by enabling users to share their trained models:

1. **Local Model Export**: Saves trained models as downloadable ZIP files
2. **HuggingFace Hub Upload**: Directly uploads models to the SaprotHub collection on HuggingFace
3. **Model Metadata**: Captures essential information about the model's purpose and performance

This feature helps build a growing ecosystem of protein language models for various tasks.

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:433-470]()

## User Experience Considerations

The ColabSaprot interface incorporates several design elements to enhance user experience:

1. **Progressive Disclosure**: Shows only relevant options based on the user's current task
2. **Visual Feedback**: Provides progress indicators for long-running operations
3. **Error Handling**: Includes comprehensive error checks and user-friendly error messages
4. **Resource Management**: Monitors and optimizes GPU memory usage

These considerations help make the interface accessible to biologists with varying levels of computational expertise.

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:64-73]()
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:37-53]()

## Specialized Interfaces

While ColabSaprot is the primary interface, SaprotHub also includes specialized interfaces for specific use cases:

1. **ColabProtT5**: Focused on the ProtT5 protein language model
2. **ColabProTrek**: Specialized for protein trajectory analysis

These interfaces follow similar design principles but are optimized for their specific model architectures and use cases. Users who have specific needs in these areas may prefer these specialized interfaces.

For more information about these specialized interfaces, see [Alternative Interfaces: ColabProtT5 and ColabProTrek](#2.4).

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:46-59]()

## Version Considerations

The SaprotHub repository contains two versions of the ColabSaprot interface:

1. **SaprotHub.ipynb**: The original version
2. **SaprotHub_v2.ipynb**: A newer version with improved user interface and functionality

Users are encouraged to use the newer version for the best experience, as it includes various improvements and fixes.

Sources:
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:9-10]()
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:6-27]()

## Conclusion

The ColabSaprot Interface serves as the primary entry point for biologists to access and leverage protein language models through SaprotHub. Its user-friendly design, flexible input methods, and comprehensive functionality make it an essential tool for democratizing protein modeling capabilities. By removing technical barriers, it enables researchers to focus on their biological questions rather than the complexities of machine learning implementation.

# Page: Data Input Methods

# Data Input Methods

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/training_curve_cls.png](Figure/training_curve_cls.png)
- [Figure/training_curve_reg.png](Figure/training_curve_reg.png)
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)
- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py)

</details>



This page details the various methods for inputting protein data into the SaprotHub framework. Whether you're training a new model or making predictions with existing models, understanding these data input options is essential. For information about model selection and training processes, see [Model Selection and Training](#2.2).

## Overview of Data Input Methods

SaprotHub provides a flexible system for inputting protein data in various formats, accommodating different research needs and data availability scenarios. The system supports multiple input types ranging from raw sequences to 3D structure files.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Types"
        AASeq["Amino Acid (AA) Sequences"]
        SASeq["Structure-Aware (SA) Sequences"]
        Structures["PDB/CIF Structure Files"]
        UniProtIDs["UniProt IDs"]
        PreDatasets["Pre-prepared Datasets"]
    end

    subgraph "Cardinality"
        Single["Single Instance"]
        Multiple["Multiple Instances"]
        Pairs["Sequence/Structure Pairs"]
        PairsMultiple["Multiple Pairs"]
    end

    AASeq --> Single
    AASeq --> Multiple
    AASeq --> Pairs
    AASeq --> PairsMultiple
    
    SASeq --> Single
    SASeq --> Multiple
    SASeq --> Pairs
    SASeq --> PairsMultiple
    
    Structures --> Single
    Structures --> Multiple
    Structures --> Pairs
    Structures --> PairsMultiple
    
    UniProtIDs --> Single
    UniProtIDs --> Multiple
    UniProtIDs --> Pairs
    UniProtIDs --> PairsMultiple
    
    PreDatasets --> Single
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:252-268](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:268-284]()

## Supported Data Types

The following table shows all data types supported by SaprotHub and their compatibility with different task types:

| Data Type | Classification | Regression | Token Classification | Pair Classification | Pair Regression |
|-----------|:-------------:|:----------:|:--------------------:|:-------------------:|:---------------:|
| Single AA Sequence | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Single SA Sequence | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Single UniProt ID | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Single PDB/CIF Structure | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Multiple AA Sequences | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Multiple SA Sequences | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Multiple UniProt IDs | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| Multiple PDB/CIF Structures | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | - | - |
| A pair of AA Sequences | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| A pair of SA Sequences | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| A pair of UniProt IDs | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| A pair of PDB/CIF Structures | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| Multiple pairs of AA Sequences | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| Multiple pairs of SA Sequences | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| Multiple pairs of UniProt IDs | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| Multiple pairs of PDB/CIF Structures | - | - | - | ✓ | ✓ |
| SaprotHub Dataset | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:290-312](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:306-328]()

## Data Processing Pipeline

The data processing pipeline converts raw inputs into formats suitable for model training or prediction:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["User Input Data"] --> DataType{"Data Type?"}
    
    DataType -->|"AA Sequence"| AASeq["Amino Acid Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"SA Sequence"| SASeq["Structure-Aware Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"UniProt ID"| UniProt["UniProt Identifier"]
    DataType -->|"PDB/CIF Structure"| PDBStruct["Protein Structure"]
    DataType -->|"Multiple Sequences"| MultiSeq["Multiple Sequences CSV"]
    DataType -->|"Multiple Structures"| MultiStruct["Multiple Structures CSV/ZIP"]
    DataType -->|"Pair Sequences"| PairSeq["Sequence Pairs"]
    
    AASeq --> Tokenization["Sequence Tokenization"]
    SASeq --> Tokenization
    
    UniProt --> |"Download Structure"| AlphaFold["AlphaFold DB"]
    AlphaFold --> ExtractChain["Extract Chain"]
    
    PDBStruct --> ExtractChain
    ExtractChain --> Foldseek["Foldseek Utility"]
    
    MultiSeq --> ProcessCSV["Process CSV File"]
    MultiStruct --> ProcessCSV
    PairSeq --> ProcessCSV
    
    Foldseek --> SAConversion["Convert to SA Sequence"]
    SAConversion --> Tokenization
    
    ProcessCSV --> BatchProcessing["Batch Processing"]
    BatchProcessing --> Tokenization
    
    Tokenization --> LMDB["LMDB Database"]
    LMDB --> ModelInput["Ready for Model Input"]
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:574-714](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:586-714](), [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:12-87]()

## Sequence-Based Inputs

### Single AA Sequence

Users can enter a single amino acid sequence directly into the text field. The sequence should only contain standard amino acid characters (A, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, K, L, M, N, P, Q, R, S, T, V, W, Y).

Example:
```
MSKGEELFTGVVPILVELDGDVNGHKFSVSGEGEGDATYGKLTLKFICTTGKLPVPWPTLVTTFSYGVQCFSRYPDHMKQHDFFKSAMPEGYVQERTIFFKDDGNYKTRAEVKFEGDTLVNRIELKGIDFKEDGNILGHKLEYNYNSHNVYIMADKQKNGIKVNFKIRHNIEDGSVQLADHYQQNTPIGDGPVLLPDNHYLSTQSALSKDPNEKRDHMVLLEFVTAAGITLGMDELYK
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:578-587](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:589-597]()

### Multiple AA Sequences via CSV

For batch processing, sequences can be uploaded in a CSV file with the following structure:

| protein | label | stage |
|---------|-------|-------|
| MSKGEE... | 1 | train |
| MADKQK... | 0 | valid |
| ... | ... | ... |

The `protein` column contains amino acid sequences, `label` contains target values, and `stage` indicates whether each sample belongs to the training, validation, or testing set.

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:613-633](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:614-635]()

## Structure-Based Inputs

### Structure-Aware (SA) Sequences

Structure-aware sequences incorporate structural information using a specialized vocabulary derived from Foldseek. They combine amino acid information with structural features into a unified sequence representation.

Example:
```
Mpqnwepadhngvskyltlsficttgklpvpwptlvttfsygvqcfsrypdhmkqhdffksampegyvqertiffkddgnyktraevkfegdtlvnrielkgidfkedgnilghkleynynshnvyimadkqkngikvnfkirhniedgsvqladhyqqntpigdgpvllpdnhylstqsalskdpnekrdhmvllefvtaagitlgmdelyk
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:587-596](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:589-597]()

### Single PDB/CIF Structure

Users can upload Protein Data Bank (PDB) or Crystallographic Information File (CIF) files. The system will:

1. Extract the specified chain (default is "A")
2. Run Foldseek to analyze the structure
3. Generate an SA sequence representation
4. For AlphaFold2 structures, low-confidence regions can be masked based on pLDDT scores

The internal process uses the `get_struc_seq` function from the Foldseek utility:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PDBFile["PDB/CIF File"] --> ExtractChain["Extract Specified Chain"]
    ExtractChain --> RunFoldseek["Run Foldseek structureto3didescriptor"]
    RunFoldseek --> IsAF2{"Is AlphaFold2 Structure?"}
    
    IsAF2 -->|"Yes"| ExtractpLDDT["Extract pLDDT Scores"]
    ExtractpLDDT --> MaskLowConfidence["Mask Low Confidence Regions"]
    MaskLowConfidence --> GenerateSASeq["Generate SA Sequence"]
    
    IsAF2 -->|"No"| GenerateSASeq
    
    GenerateSASeq --> Representation["Final Structure Representation"]
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:598-610](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:600-612](), [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:12-87]()

### Multiple PDB/CIF Structures

For batch processing of structures:

1. Upload a CSV file with references to structure files (similar format to multiple sequences)
2. Upload a ZIP file containing all the referenced structure files
3. The system will process each structure using the same pipeline as for single structures

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:621-633](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:621-635]()

## Identifier-Based Inputs

### UniProt IDs

Instead of providing sequences or structures directly, users can enter UniProt IDs. The system will:

1. Automatically retrieve the corresponding structure from AlphaFold Database
2. Process the structure to extract the specified chain
3. Convert it to an SA sequence using Foldseek

Example: `P42212` (Green Fluorescent Protein)

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:578-587](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:589-597]()

### Multiple UniProt IDs via CSV

For batch processing of UniProt IDs, users can upload a CSV file with the following structure:

| uniprot_id | label | stage |
|------------|-------|-------|
| P42212 | 1 | train |
| P0DMV8 | 0 | valid |
| ... | ... | ... |

The system will retrieve structures for each ID and process them as described above.

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:613-633](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:614-635]()

## Protein-Protein Interaction Inputs

### Pair Inputs

For protein-protein interaction tasks, SaprotHub supports paired inputs:

1. **Single pairs**: Enter two sequences, structures, or UniProt IDs separately
2. **Multiple pairs via CSV**: Upload a CSV file with the following structure:

| protein_1 | protein_2 | label | stage |
|-----------|-----------|-------|-------|
| MSKGEE... | MADKQK... | 1 | train |
| P42212 | P0DMV8 | 0 | valid |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:646-668](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:648-670]()

### Structure Pairs

For structure-based protein-protein interaction tasks:

1. Upload two separate PDB/CIF files
2. Specify the chain to extract from each structure
3. The system will process both structures and prepare them for the interaction model

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:672-714](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:673-714]()

## Pre-prepared Datasets

### SaprotHub Datasets

SaprotHub provides pre-prepared datasets for various protein prediction tasks:

1. Enter a dataset ID from the SaprotHub repository (e.g., `SaProtHub/thermostability`)
2. The system will download and prepare the dataset automatically

Pre-prepared datasets are particularly useful for benchmarking or reproducing published results.

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:636-644](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:638-646]()

## Data Type Compatibility and Conversion

SaprotHub implements automatic conversions between different data types when necessary:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input Data"] --> InputDetection["Input Type Detection"]
    
    InputDetection --> AASeq["AA Sequence"]
    InputDetection --> SASeq["SA Sequence"]
    InputDetection --> UniProt["UniProt ID"]
    InputDetection --> PDBStruct["PDB/CIF Structure"]
    
    AASeq --> TokenizeAA["Tokenize AA Sequence"]
    SASeq --> TokenizeSA["Tokenize SA Sequence"]
    
    UniProt --> DownloadAF["Download from AlphaFold DB"]
    DownloadAF --> PDBStruct
    
    PDBStruct --> ExtractChain["Extract Chain"]
    ExtractChain --> RunFoldseek["Run Foldseek"]
    RunFoldseek --> GenerateSASeq["Generate SA Sequence"]
    GenerateSASeq --> TokenizeSA
    
    TokenizeAA --> TaskType{"Task Type?"}
    TokenizeSA --> TaskType
    
    TaskType -->|"Classification/\nRegression/\nToken Classification"| SingleProtein["Single Protein Processing"]
    TaskType -->|"Pair Classification/\nPair Regression"| PairProtein["Protein Pair Processing"]
    
    SingleProtein --> FeatureExtraction["Feature Extraction"]
    PairProtein --> PairFeatureExtraction["Pair Feature Extraction"]
    
    FeatureExtraction --> ModelInput["Model Input"]
    PairFeatureExtraction --> ModelInput
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:312-329](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:327-345](), [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:12-87]()

## Best Practices for Data Input

1. **Sequence quality**: Ensure sequences don't contain non-standard amino acids or invalid characters
2. **Structure selection**: For structures, select biologically relevant chains
3. **CSV formatting**: Verify CSV files have the correct column names and proper formatting
4. **Batch size management**: For large datasets, consider splitting into manageable batches
5. **pLDDT thresholds**: When using AlphaFold2 structures, consider adjusting the pLDDT threshold (default is 70) based on your confidence requirements

The `input_raw_data_by_data_type` function is the central implementation that handles all these input methods in the SaprotHub system.

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:574-714](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:586-714]()

---

# Page: Model Selection and Training

# Model Selection and Training

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/training_curve_cls.png](Figure/training_curve_cls.png)
- [Figure/training_curve_reg.png](Figure/training_curve_reg.png)
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)
- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This guide explains how to select and train protein language models using the ColabSaprot interface. It covers model selection based on tasks, configuring training parameters, and monitoring the training process. For uploading and sharing your trained models, see [Model Uploading and Sharing](#2.3), and for specialized interfaces for specific protein models, see [Alternative Interfaces](#2.4).

## Model Selection Process

The ColabSaprot interface allows users to select appropriate models based on their biological task requirements. The selection process follows a structured workflow that guides users from task definition to model configuration.

### Available Task Types

SaprotHub provides models for five distinct protein prediction tasks:

| Task Type | Internal Name | Description |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| Protein-level Classification | `classification` | Predicts categorical properties of entire proteins |
| Residue-level Classification | `token_classification` | Predicts properties for individual amino acid residues |
| Protein-level Regression | `regression` | Predicts continuous values for entire proteins |
| Protein-protein Classification | `pair_classification` | Predicts categorical properties for protein pairs |
| Protein-protein Regression | `pair_regression` | Predicts continuous values for protein pairs |

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:290-296]()

### Model Selection Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start("Start") --> DefineTask["Define Task Type"]
    DefineTask --> InputData["Input Data Type Selection"]
    InputData --> ModelSize["Select Model Size"]
    ModelSize --> TrainingParams["Set Training Parameters"]
    TrainingParams --> Train["Train Model"]
    Train --> Evaluate["Evaluate Results"]
    Evaluate --> Save["Save Model"]
    
    subgraph "Task Types"
    TClass["Protein-level Classification"]
    TReg["Protein-level Regression"]
    TToken["Residue-level Classification"]
    TPairClass["Protein-protein Classification"]
    TPairReg["Protein-protein Regression"]
    end

    subgraph "Model Sizes"
    Size35M["SaProt 35M (small)"]
    Size650M["SaProt 650M (large)"]
    end
    
    DefineTask -.-> TClass
    DefineTask -.-> TReg
    DefineTask -.-> TToken
    DefineTask -.-> TPairClass
    DefineTask -.-> TPairReg
    
    ModelSize -.-> Size35M
    ModelSize -.-> Size650M
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:290-296](), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:307-319]()

## Training Data Preparation

Before training, users need to prepare their data in the appropriate format. ColabSaprot supports various data input methods, which are handled differently based on the task type.

### Supported Data Types

The system supports 17 data types, broadly categorized into:

- Single-sequence inputs (AA, SA, UniProt ID, PDB/CIF Structure)
- Pair-sequence inputs (pairs of AA, SA, UniProt ID, PDB/CIF Structure)  
- Multiple-sequence inputs (multiple instances of the above)
- SaprotHub datasets (pre-prepared datasets from the community)

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:252-268](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:268-284]()

### Data Type and Task Compatibility

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Data["Input Data"] --> DataType{"Data Type?"}
    
    DataType -->|"AA Sequence(s)" aa_seq| AAProcess["Process Amino Acid Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"SA Sequence(s)" sa_seq| SAProcess["Process Structure-Aware Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"Structure(s)" struct| StructProcess["Convert Structure to SA Sequence"]
    DataType -->|"UniProt ID(s)" uniprot| FetchStruct["Fetch Structure from AlphaFold DB"]
    
    FetchStruct --> StructProcess
    
    AAProcess --> |"For classification/\nregression"| SingleModel["Single Sequence Model"]
    SAProcess --> |"For classification/\nregression"| SingleModel
    
    AAProcess --> |"For pair tasks"| PairModel["Pair Sequence Model"]
    SAProcess --> |"For pair tasks"| PairModel
    
    SingleModel --> TaskType{"Task Type?"}
    PairModel --> PairTaskType{"Pair Task Type?"}
    
    TaskType -->|"classification"| ClassModel["Classification Model"]
    TaskType -->|"regression"| RegModel["Regression Model"]
    TaskType -->|"token_classification"| TokenModel["Token Classification Model"]
    
    PairTaskType -->|"pair_classification"| PairClassModel["Pair Classification Model"]
    PairTaskType -->|"pair_regression"| PairRegModel["Pair Regression Model"]
    
    subgraph "Data Validation"
    CheckCompat["Check Task-Data Compatibility"]
    ValidateFormat["Validate Data Format"]
    end
    
    DataType --> CheckCompat
    CheckCompat --> ValidateFormat
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:570-572](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:581-583]()

### Data Processing Flow

When you input data into ColabSaprot, it goes through a processing pipeline before being used for training:

1. Data validation to ensure compatibility with the selected task
2. Conversion to appropriate sequence format (AA or SA)
3. Storage in LMDB format for efficient training
4. Dataset splitting into train, validation, and test sets

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:534-536](), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:553-566](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:547-550]()

## Model Architecture Selection

SaprotHub provides pre-trained protein language models (PLMs) in different sizes, which serve as the foundation for training task-specific models.

### Available Model Sizes

| Model | Parameters | Suitable For | GPU Requirement |
|-------|------------|--------------|-----------------|
| SaProt 35M | 35 million | Simple tasks, faster training | T4 (Free tier) |
| SaProt 650M | 650 million | Complex tasks, better performance | L4/A100 (Colab Pro) |

### Model Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "SaProt Base Models"
        PLM["Pre-trained Language Model"]
        PLM -->|"35M Parameters"| SmallModel["SaProt 35M"]
        PLM -->|"650M Parameters"| LargeModel["SaProt 650M"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Task-specific Models"
        SmallModel --> SaprotBaseModel["SaprotBaseModel"]
        LargeModel --> SaprotBaseModel
        
        SaprotBaseModel --> Classification["SaprotClassificationModel"]
        SaprotBaseModel --> Regression["SaprotRegressionModel"]
        SaprotBaseModel --> TokenClassification["SaprotTokenClassificationModel"]
        SaprotBaseModel --> PairClassification["SaprotPairClassificationModel"]
        SaprotBaseModel --> PairRegression["SaprotPairRegressionModel"]
    end
    
    subgraph "LoRA Adaptation Layer"
        Classification --> LoRAAdapter["LoRA Adapter"]
        Regression --> LoRAAdapter
        TokenClassification --> LoRAAdapter
        PairClassification --> LoRAAdapter
        PairRegression --> LoRAAdapter
    end
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:298-310](), [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb:309-321]()

## Training Configuration

Training a model in ColabSaprot requires setting several parameters that influence model performance and training efficiency.

### Essential Training Parameters

| Parameter | Description | Typical Values |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| Base Model | Size of the pre-trained model | 35M, 650M |
| Learning Rate | Step size for optimization | 1e-4 to 1e-3 |
| Batch Size | Number of samples processed together | 16-128 |
| Epochs | Number of training iterations | 10-100 |
| LoRA Rank | Rank of Low-Rank Adaptation matrices | 8, 16, 32 |
| LoRA Alpha | Scaling factor for LoRA | 16, 32 |
| Scheduler Type | Learning rate scheduling strategy | Linear, Cosine |

### Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)

SaprotHub uses Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, which significantly reduces memory requirements and speeds up training. This is particularly important for training on GPU resources with limited memory, such as those available in Google Colab.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "LoRA Fine-Tuning Process"
        PreTrainedModel["Pre-trained SaProt Model"] --> FrozenParams["Frozen Parameters"]
        PreTrainedModel --> LoRAParams["LoRA Parameters (trainable)"]
        
        FrozenParams --> ForwardPass["Forward Pass"]
        LoRAParams --> ForwardPass
        
        ForwardPass --> Loss["Loss Calculation"]
        Loss --> Backprop["Backpropagation"]
        
        Backprop --> UpdateLoRA["Update LoRA Parameters"]
        UpdateLoRA --> NextBatch["Next Batch"]
        NextBatch -->|"Until convergence"| ForwardPass
    end
    
    subgraph "Memory Efficiency"
        LoRAParams -->|"Small memory footprint"| EfficientTraining["Efficient Training"]
        FrozenParams -->|"No gradients stored"| EfficientTraining
    end
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py:1-133]()

## Training Process

Once the model and parameters are selected, the training process can begin. This section describes the training workflow and monitoring.

### Training Workflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant ColabSaprot
    participant DataProcessor
    participant SaprotModel
    participant TrainingLoop
    participant Evaluation
    
    User->>ColabSaprot: Select task type
    User->>ColabSaprot: Upload/input data
    User->>ColabSaprot: Configure training parameters
    ColabSaprot->>DataProcessor: Process input data
    DataProcessor->>ColabSaprot: Create LMDB dataset
    ColabSaprot->>SaprotModel: Initialize model
    ColabSaprot->>SaprotModel: Initialize LoRA adaptation
    ColabSaprot->>TrainingLoop: Start training
    
    loop Each Epoch
        TrainingLoop->>SaprotModel: Forward pass
        SaprotModel->>TrainingLoop: Calculate loss
        TrainingLoop->>SaprotModel: Backpropagation & update
        TrainingLoop->>Evaluation: Periodic validation
        Evaluation->>TrainingLoop: Report metrics
        TrainingLoop->>ColabSaprot: Update progress
    end
    
    TrainingLoop->>ColabSaprot: Final evaluation
    ColabSaprot->>User: Display metrics
    ColabSaprot->>User: Save trained model
```

### Training Monitoring

During training, ColabSaprot provides real-time visualization of training metrics:

1. **Loss curves**: Training and validation loss over epochs
2. **Performance metrics**: 
   - For classification: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score
   - For regression: mean squared error, Pearson correlation
   - For token classification: per-token accuracy, F1-score
   - For pair tasks: pair-wise metrics

### Handling Training Issues

Common training issues and their solutions:

1. **Out of memory errors**: Reduce batch size or use a smaller model (35M instead of 650M)
2. **Overfitting**: Apply early stopping or reduce model capacity
3. **Poor convergence**: Adjust learning rate or increase training epochs
4. **Colab disconnection**: Use Colab Pro+ for extended runtime or save checkpoints frequently

## Model Evaluation

After training, it's important to evaluate the model's performance on test data to ensure it generalizes well to unseen examples.

### Evaluation Metrics

The evaluation metrics depend on the task type:

| Task Type | Primary Metrics | Secondary Metrics |
|-----------|----------------|-------------------|
| Classification | Accuracy, F1-score | Precision, Recall, AUC |
| Regression | Mean Squared Error, R² | Pearson Correlation, RMSE |
| Token Classification | Token-wise F1-score | Per-class metrics |
| Pair Classification | Accuracy, F1-score | Precision, Recall |
| Pair Regression | Mean Squared Error, R² | Pearson Correlation |

### Results Interpretation

ColabSaprot provides visualization tools to help interpret model results:

1. **Confusion matrices** for classification tasks
2. **Scatter plots** for regression tasks
3. **Residue-level highlighting** for token classification tasks
4. **Protein structure visualization** for structure-based predictions

## Saving and Exporting Models

Once training is complete, you can save your model for future use or sharing with the community.

### Saving Options

1. **Local saving**: Save the adapter to your local machine for future use
2. **Upload to SaprotHub**: Share your model with the community (requires a HuggingFace account)

### Model Packaging

The saved model will include:

1. **LoRA adapter weights**: The fine-tuned parameters specific to your task
2. **Configuration file**: Model architecture and training parameters
3. **Metadata**: Task description, performance metrics, and data information

For detailed instructions on how to upload and share your models, see [Model Uploading and Sharing](#2.3).

## Conclusion

This guide covered the process of selecting and training protein language models in ColabSaprot. By following these steps, you can develop custom models for various protein prediction tasks without deep machine learning expertise. The parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach enables effective training even on limited computational resources, making advanced protein modeling accessible to all biologists.

For specific tasks and applications of the trained models, refer to other pages in this wiki.

---

# Page: Model Uploading and Sharing

# Model Uploading and Sharing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/training_curve_cls.png](Figure/training_curve_cls.png)
- [Figure/training_curve_reg.png](Figure/training_curve_reg.png)
- [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub.ipynb)
- [colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb](colab/SaprotHub_v2.ipynb)
- [saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py](saprot/utils/foldseek_util.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document details how to save, upload, and share trained protein language models with the scientific community through SaprotHub. It covers the process of saving models locally, uploading models from your computer, sharing models via HuggingFace Hub, and using models shared by peers. 

For information about training models, please refer to [Model Selection and Training](#2.2). For details on specialized interfaces, see [Alternative Interfaces: ColabProtT5 and ColabProTrek](#2.4).

## Model Structure Overview

SaprotHub uses Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to create small, task-specific adapters that can be easily shared without distributing the entire pre-trained protein language model.

### Model Adapter Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    PTM["Pre-trained Protein Language Model"] -->|Fine-tuned with| LoRA["LoRA Technique"]
    LoRA -->|Creates| Adapter["Task-specific Adapter"]
    
    Adapter -->|Saved in| LocalStorage[("Local Storage\nadapters/{task_type}/")]
    Adapter -->|Shared on| HFHub[("HuggingFace Hub\nSaprotHub Organization")]
    
    subgraph "Adapter Types"
        ClsAdapter["Classification Adapter"]
        RegAdapter["Regression Adapter"] 
        TokenAdapter["Token Classification Adapter"]
        PairClsAdapter["Pair Classification Adapter"]
        PairRegAdapter["Pair Regression Adapter"]
    end
    
    Adapter --> ClsAdapter
    Adapter --> RegAdapter
    Adapter --> TokenAdapter
    Adapter --> PairClsAdapter
    Adapter --> PairRegAdapter
```

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:149-167]()

## Local Model Storage

After training, models are automatically saved in task-specific directories within the SaprotHub environment:

```
adapters/<task_type>/Local/<model_name>/
```

Where `<task_type>` is one of:
- `classification`: For protein-level classification tasks
- `regression`: For protein-level regression tasks
- `token_classification`: For residue-level (per-amino-acid) classification tasks
- `pair_classification`: For protein-protein interaction classification tasks
- `pair_regression`: For protein-protein interaction regression tasks

Each adapter directory contains essential files:
- `adapter_model.bin`: The trained adapter weights
- `adapter_config.json`: Configuration including task type, model size, and training parameters

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:149-167](), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:307-326]()

## Managing Models

### Downloading Models to Your Computer

After training a model in ColabSaprot, you can download it to your local computer for backup or to use in a different session:

1. Navigate to the model directory in the file explorer (typically in `/content/SaprotHub/adapters/<task_type>/Local/<model_name>/`)
2. Right-click on the directory and select "Download"
3. The model will be downloaded as a zip file to your computer

### Uploading Models from Your Computer

To use a model saved on your local computer:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant ColabSaprot as "ColabSaprot Interface"
    participant LocalStorage as "Local Storage"
    
    User->>ColabSaprot: Select "Saved in your local computer"
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Prompt for model file
    User->>ColabSaprot: Upload "Model-<task_name>-<model_size>.zip"
    ColabSaprot->>ColabSaprot: Extract .zip file
    ColabSaprot->>LocalStorage: Store in adapters/<task_type>/Local/
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Model available for use
```

1. Prepare your model as a `.zip` file with the format `Model-<task_name>-<model_size>.zip`
2. When selecting a model, choose "Saved in your local computer" option
3. Upload the `.zip` file when prompted
4. The model will be extracted and stored in the appropriate directory for use

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:447-456]()

## Sharing Models on HuggingFace Hub

To share your model with the scientific community:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant ColabSaprot as "ColabSaprot Interface"
    participant HFHub as "HuggingFace Hub"
    
    User->>ColabSaprot: Select "Contribute to SaprotHub"
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Prompt for model details
    User->>ColabSaprot: Provide metadata (task type, description)
    ColabSaprot->>HFHub: Upload adapter files
    HFHub-->>ColabSaprot: Return model URL
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Display model URL for sharing
```

1. After training a model in ColabSaprot, use the "Contribute to SaprotHub" option
2. Provide metadata about your model:
   - Model name
   - Task type
   - Description
   - Training data source
   - Performance metrics
3. The model will be uploaded to the SaprotHub organization on HuggingFace Hub
4. You'll receive a URL that you can share with collaborators and the community

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:54]()

## Using Shared Models

### Using Models from HuggingFace Hub

To use models shared by others in the scientific community:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant ColabSaprot as "ColabSaprot Interface"
    participant HFHub as "HuggingFace Hub"
    
    User->>ColabSaprot: Select "Shared by peers on SaprotHub"
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Prompt for Model ID
    User->>ColabSaprot: Enter SaprotHub Model ID
    ColabSaprot->>HFHub: Request model download
    HFHub-->>ColabSaprot: Download adapter files
    ColabSaprot->>ColabSaprot: Load model
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Model ready for use
```

1. Find the model ID on the [SaprotHub organization page](https://huggingface.co/SaProtHub)
2. When selecting a model, choose "Shared by peers on SaprotHub" option
3. Enter the model ID in the text field
4. The model will be automatically downloaded and loaded for use

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:444-446]()

### Using Models from Local Storage

To use a previously trained or uploaded model:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant ColabSaprot as "ColabSaprot Interface"
    participant LocalStorage as "Local Storage"
    
    User->>ColabSaprot: Select "Trained by yourself on ColabSaprot"
    ColabSaprot->>LocalStorage: Get available models
    LocalStorage-->>ColabSaprot: Return model list
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Display model dropdown
    User->>ColabSaprot: Select model
    ColabSaprot->>LocalStorage: Load selected model
    ColabSaprot-->>User: Model ready for use
```

1. When selecting a model, choose "Trained by yourself on ColabSaprot" option
2. Select the model from the dropdown list
3. The model will be loaded for use

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:441-443](), [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:363-375]()

## Technical Details and Best Practices

### Model Format Requirements

When sharing models, ensure your adapter follows these requirements:

1. The adapter must include `adapter_model.bin` and `adapter_config.json`
2. The adapter configuration must specify the task type, model size, and other parameters
3. For maximum compatibility, use the recommended LoRA configuration from SaprotHub

### Best Practices for Model Sharing

1. **Clear Documentation**: Provide detailed descriptions of your model's purpose, training data, and intended use cases
2. **Performance Metrics**: Include metrics (accuracy, F1 score, etc.) to help users evaluate model suitability
3. **Attribution**: Cite original data sources used for training
4. **Versioning**: Clearly indicate model versions if you update your shared models
5. **License Information**: Specify any license restrictions on your model

## Using Multiple Models

SaprotHub also supports using multiple models for ensemble predictions:

1. When selecting models, choose "Multi-models on ColabSaprot" for local models or "Multi-models on SaprotHub" for shared models
2. For local models, select multiple models using Ctrl/Shift + click
3. For HuggingFace models, enter multiple model IDs separated by commas
4. The interface will load all selected models and enable ensemble prediction functionality

Sources: [colab/SaprotHub.ipynb:459-481]()

---

This documentation provides a comprehensive guide to model uploading and sharing in SaprotHub. By following these steps, you can effectively save, share, and use protein language models to advance collaborative research in the biological community.

# Page: Alternative Interfaces: ColabProtT5 and ColabProTrek

# Alternative Interfaces: ColabProtT5 and ColabProTrek

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb](colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb)
- [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb](colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb)

</details>



This page introduces two specialized Colab-based interfaces within the SaprotHub ecosystem: ColabProtT5 and ColabProTrek. These interfaces provide user-friendly access to specific protein language models (PLMs) and are designed to make advanced protein modeling accessible to biologists. For information about the primary SaprotHub interface, see [ColabSaprot Interface](#2).

## 1. Interface Overview

ColabProtT5 and ColabProTrek are specialized notebook interfaces that provide streamlined access to specific protein language models. They share the same underlying architecture as the main SaprotHub interface but are tailored for particular protein language models.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    User[Researcher/Biologist] --> Interfaces

    subgraph "Interfaces"
        Interfaces[SaprotHub Interfaces]
        Interfaces --> ColabSaprot[Main SaprotHub Interface]
        Interfaces --> ColabProtT5[ColabProtT5]
        Interfaces --> ColabProTrek[ColabProTrek]
    end

    ColabProtT5 --> ProtT5[ProtT5 Model]
    ColabProTrek --> ProTrek[ProTrek Model]

    subgraph "Functionality"
        Train[Model Training]
        Predict[Prediction]
        Share[Model Sharing]
    end

    ColabProtT5 --> Functionality
    ColabProTrek --> Functionality

    subgraph "Models"
        ProtT5 --> |1.2B parameters|T5Encoder["Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_half_uniref50-enc"]
        ProTrek --> |35M parameters|Trek35M["ProTrekHub/Protein_Encoder_35M"]
        ProTrek --> |650M parameters|Trek650M["ProTrekHub/Protein_Encoder_650M"]
    end
```

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:9-29](), [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:9-29]()

### 1.1 Key Differences

| Feature | ColabProtT5 | ColabProTrek |
|---------|-------------|-------------|
| Underlying Model | ProtT5 (1.2B parameters) | ProTrek (35M or 650M parameters) |
| Model Hub | T5Hub | ProTrekHub |
| GPU Requirements | Requires A100 GPU | Works with standard GPUs |
| Specialized For | Powerful encodings via T5 architecture | Sequence-structure-function pairwise searches |
| Model Path | `Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_half_uniref50-enc` | `ProTrekHub/Protein_Encoder_35M` or `ProTrekHub/Protein_Encoder_650M` |

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:52-75](), [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:52-75]()

## 2. Installation and Setup

Both interfaces follow a similar installation process, but with model-specific dependencies.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start[Start Installation] --> CheckGPU["Check GPU Availability"]
    CheckGPU --> |"GPU Available"| InstallDeps["Install Dependencies"]
    CheckGPU --> |"No GPU"| Error["Error: GPU Required"]
    
    InstallDeps --> CloneRepo["Clone SaprotHub Repository"]
    CloneRepo --> CreateDirs["Create Required Directories"]
    CreateDirs --> DownloadModel["Download Base Model"]
    
    subgraph "Environment Setup (Both Interfaces)"
        CreateDirs --> |Create|LMDB["LMDB Directory"]
        CreateDirs --> |Create|Adapters["Adapters Directory"]
        CreateDirs --> |Create|Structures["Structures Directory"]
        CreateDirs --> |Create|Datasets["Datasets Directory"]
        CreateDirs --> |Create|Output["Output Directory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Download"
        DownloadModel --> |"ColabProtT5"|ProtT5["Download ProtT5 (1.2B)"]
        DownloadModel --> |"ColabProTrek"|ProTrek["Download ProTrek (35M/650M)"]
    end
    
    ProtT5 --> Complete["Installation Complete"]
    ProTrek --> Complete
```

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:79-244](), [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:79-244]()

### 2.1 GPU Requirements

ColabProtT5 has stricter GPU requirements due to the size of the ProtT5 model:

```
Due to ProtT5's encoder containing 1.2B parameters, please ensure you run it on Colab Pro with an L4 or A100 GPU, otherwise, it will result in out of memory errors.
```

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:60-62]()

ProTrek models are smaller and can run on standard GPUs available in Colab.

## 3. Training Workflow

Both interfaces support the same training workflow with minor differences in the model selection options.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "1. Task Configuration"
        TaskName["Task Name"]
        TaskType["Task Type:
        - Protein-level Classification
        - Protein-level Regression
        - Residue-level Classification
        - Protein-protein Classification (ProTrek only)
        - Protein-protein Regression (ProTrek only)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "2. Model Selection"
        ProtT5Model["ColabProtT5:
        - Pretrained ProtT5 Encoder (1.2B)
        - Existing trained models"]
        
        ProTrekModel["ColabProTrek:
        - Official pretrained ProTrek (35M)
        - Official pretrained ProTrek (650M)
        - Existing trained models"]
    end
    
    subgraph "3. Dataset Selection"
        DataType["Data Type:
        - Multiple AA Sequences
        - Multiple SA Sequences
        - Multiple UniProt IDs
        - Multiple pairs (ProTrek only)"]
        UploadData["Upload Dataset CSV"]
    end
    
    subgraph "4. Training Configuration"
        BatchSize["Batch Size (Adaptive/Manual)"]
        Epochs["Max Epochs"]
        LearningRate["Learning Rate"]
    end
    
    TaskConfiguration --> ModelSelection
    ModelSelection --> DatasetSelection
    DatasetSelection --> TrainingConfiguration
    TrainingConfiguration --> StartTraining["Start Training"]
    
    StartTraining --> LoRA["LoRA Fine-tuning"]
    LoRA --> SaveModel["Save Adapter Model"]
    SaveModel --> DownloadModel["Download Model to Local Computer"]
```

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:1253-1304](), [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:1306-1749](), [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:1255-1307](), [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:1310-1751]()
