## 6. Key Implementation Differences

While both interfaces share the same overall architecture, there are important implementation differences:

### 6.1 Model-specific Configurations

#### ColabProtT5
- Uses ProtT5 encoder (`Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_half_uniref50-enc`)
- Model configuration path: `protT5/protT5_classification_model`
- Dataset configuration path: `protT5/protT5_classification_dataset`

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:274-286]()

#### ColabProTrek
- Uses ProTrek models (`ProTrekHub/Protein_Encoder_35M` or `ProTrekHub/Protein_Encoder_650M`)
- Model configuration path: `saprot/saprot_classification_model`
- Dataset configuration path: `saprot/saprot_classification_dataset`

Sources: [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:276-288]()

### 6.2 Protein Pair Task Support

While both interfaces provide similar functionalities, ColabProTrek has more explicit support for protein pair tasks, including:
- Protein-protein classification
- Protein-protein regression
- Processing of protein pair sequences

This makes ColabProTrek particularly suited for tasks involving protein interactions.

Sources: [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:1391-1394]()

## 7. When to Choose Each Interface

| Use Case | Recommended Interface |
|----------|----------------------|
| When maximum model capacity is needed | ColabProtT5 (1.2B parameters) |
| When working with limited computing resources | ColabProTrek (35M model) |
| For protein-protein interaction tasks | ColabProTrek |
| For sequence annotation tasks | Either (task-dependent) |
| When A100 GPU is not available | ColabProTrek |
| When fine-tuning on very complex tasks | ColabProtT5 |

## 8. Integration with the SaprotHub Ecosystem

Both interfaces are designed to integrate with the larger SaprotHub system:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "SaprotHub Ecosystem"
        ColabSaprot["Main SaprotHub Interface"]
        ColabProtT5["ColabProtT5 Interface"]
        ColabProTrek["ColabProTrek Interface"]
        
        SharedComponents["Shared Components:
        - LMDB Dataset System
        - Model Training Pipeline
        - LoRA Adapters
        - Prediction System"]
    end
    
    SharedComponents --- ColabSaprot
    SharedComponents --- ColabProtT5
    SharedComponents --- ColabProTrek
    
    ColabSaprot --> |"Model Exchange"|T5Hub["T5Hub"]
    ColabProtT5 --> |"Model Exchange"|T5Hub
    ColabProTrek --> |"Model Exchange"|ProTrekHub["ProTrekHub"]
    
    T5Hub <--> |"Cross-platform Model Sharing"|ProTrekHub
    
    Users["Biologists/Researchers"] --> |"Choose Interface Based on Needs"|SaprotHub
```

Sources: [colab/ColabProtT5.ipynb:18-20](), [colab/ColabProTrek.ipynb:22-24]()

Both interfaces leverage the same underlying infrastructure, enabling users to choose the most appropriate interface for their specific needs while maintaining compatibility with the broader SaprotHub ecosystem.

# Page: Model Architecture

# Model Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [saprot/model/protT5/base.py](saprot/model/protT5/base.py)

- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](saprot/model/saprot/base.py)
- [saprot/scripts/training.py](saprot/scripts/training.py)

This page documents the technical architecture of the protein language models (PLMs) in SaprotHub. It covers the model hierarchy, base model implementations, task-specific variants, and how Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) is integrated via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). For information about training these models, see [Training Pipeline](#5) and for data processing details, see [Data Processing](#4).

## Model Hierarchy Overview

SaprotHub implements a modular model architecture that follows a clear inheritance hierarchy. At the core is an abstract base class that defines the model interface, with specialized implementations for different protein language model types and prediction tasks.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AbstractModel {
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +test_step()
        +load_checkpoint()
        +save_checkpoint()
    }
    
    AbstractModel <|-- SaprotBaseModel
    AbstractModel <|-- ProtT5BaseModel
    
    class SaprotBaseModel {
        +task: str
        +tokenizer
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
        +get_hidden_states_from_seqs()
        +add_bias_feature()
    }
    
    class ProtT5BaseModel {
        +task: str
        +tokenizer
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
        +add_bias_feature()
    }
    
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotRegressionModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotTokenClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairRegressionModel
    
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5ClassificationModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5RegressionModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5TokenClassificationModel
    
    class SaprotClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
    }
    
    class ProtT5ClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
    }
    
    class SaprotRegressionModel {
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
    }
    
    class ProtT5RegressionModel {
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
    }
    
    class SaprotTokenClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
    }
    
    class ProtT5TokenClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
    }
```

Sources: [saprot/model/abstract_model.py](), [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](), [saprot/model/protT5/base.py](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py]()

## Base Models

### AbstractModel

The `AbstractModel` class is the foundation of all models in SaprotHub. It inherits from PyTorch Lightning's `LightningModule` and defines the essential methods that all specialized models must implement.

Key responsibilities:
- Model initialization and loading from checkpoints
- Training, validation, and testing workflows
- Optimizer and learning rate scheduler configuration
- Checkpoint saving and loading
- Metric tracking and reporting

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "AbstractModel Core Components"
        Init["initialize_model()"]
        Forward["forward()"]
        Loss["loss_func()"]
        TrainStep["training_step()"]
        ValStep["validation_step()"]
        TestStep["test_step()"]
        CheckSave["save_checkpoint()"]
        CheckLoad["load_checkpoint()"]
        Metrics["initialize_metrics()"]
        Optimizers["init_optimizers()"]
    end
    
    TrainStep --> Forward --> Loss
    ValStep --> Forward --> Loss
    TestStep --> Forward --> Loss
    
    Init --> Metrics
    Init --> Optimizers
```

Sources: [saprot/model/abstract_model.py:12-406]()

### SaprotBaseModel

`SaprotBaseModel` extends `AbstractModel` and serves as the foundation for ESM-based models. It initializes the ESM model from Hugging Face transformers and provides methods for obtaining hidden representations and working with structure information.

Key features:
- ESM model initialization with configurable parameters
- Support for different tasks (classification, regression, token classification)
- LoRA integration for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
- Extraction of hidden states from sequences
- Integration of structural information via bias features

```python
# SaprotBaseModel initializes different model types based on the specified task
def initialize_model(self):
    # Initialize tokenizer
    self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(self.config_path)
    
    # Initialize different models according to task
    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(self.config_path)
    # ... then initialize the appropriate model type based on self.task
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:21-453]()

### ProtT5BaseModel

`ProtT5BaseModel` is similar to `SaprotBaseModel` but built for T5-based protein language models. It initializes the T5 model from Hugging Face transformers and provides similar functionality adapted for the T5 architecture.

Key features:
- T5 model initialization with configurable parameters
- Support for different tasks (classification, regression, token classification)
- LoRA integration for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
- Extraction of hidden states from input dictionaries
- Integration of structural information via bias features

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:27-393]()

## LoRA Integration

Both base models implement LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. LoRA adds small, trainable "adapter" modules to the pre-trained model instead of fine-tuning all parameters, significantly reducing the computational and memory requirements.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "LoRA Integration"
        LoRAConfig["LoRA Configuration"]
        TargetModules["Target Modules:
        - query/key/value attention matrices
        - feed-forward layers"]
        AdapterInit["Initialize LoRA Adapters"]
        TrainableParams["Set Trainable Parameters"]
        ForwardFunc["Modify Forward Function"]
    end
    
    LoRAConfig --> TargetModules
    TargetModules --> AdapterInit
    AdapterInit --> TrainableParams
    TrainableParams --> ForwardFunc
    
    subgraph "Multiple LoRA Support"
        MultiAdapter["Multiple Adapter Support"]
        Voting["Classification: Majority Voting"]
        Averaging["Regression: Averaging Outputs"]
    end
    
    ForwardFunc --> MultiAdapter
    MultiAdapter --> Voting
    MultiAdapter --> Averaging
```

Implementation details:
- For `SaprotBaseModel`, LoRA targets query, key, value, and dense layers
- For `ProtT5BaseModel`, LoRA targets self-attention and encoder-decoder attention components
- Both models support multiple LoRA adapters with ensemble prediction

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:74-171](), [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:79-181]()

## Task-Specific Models

SaprotHub provides specialized models for different protein prediction tasks. Each task-specific model customizes the forward pass and loss calculation for its particular needs.

### Classification Models

`ProtT5ClassificationModel` extends `ProtT5BaseModel` for sequence classification tasks.

Key features:
- Initializes a classifier head with the architecture: Linear → ReLU → Linear
- Takes sequence inputs and returns class logits
- Uses cross-entropy loss for classification
- Tracks accuracy metrics during training and evaluation

```python
# ProtT5ClassificationModel classifier initialization
def initialize_model(self):
    super().initialize_model()
    
    hidden_size = self.model.config.hidden_size
    classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
        torch.nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size),
        torch.nn.ReLU(),
        torch.nn.Linear(hidden_size, self.num_labels)
    )
    
    setattr(self.model, "classifier", classifier)
```

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:11-106]()

### Regression Models

`ProtT5RegressionModel` extends `ProtT5BaseModel` for regression tasks.

Key features:
- Initializes a regression head with the architecture: Linear → ReLU → Linear(output=1)
- Takes sequence inputs and returns scalar values
- Uses mean squared error loss
- Tracks MSE, Spearman correlation, R² score, and Pearson correlation during training and evaluation

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:10-126]()

### Token Classification Models

`ProtT5TokenClassificationModel` extends `ProtT5BaseModel` for token-level classification tasks (e.g., residue-level property prediction).

Key features:
- Initializes a token classifier head with the architecture: Linear → ReLU → Linear
- Takes sequence inputs and returns logits for each token
- Uses cross-entropy loss with support for ignored indices
- Tracks accuracy and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) during training and evaluation

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:11-166]()

## Task and Model Type Mapping

The following table shows the supported task types and their corresponding model implementations:

| Task Type | SaProt Implementation | ProtT5 Implementation | Description |
|-----------|----------------------|------------------------|-------------|
| Classification | SaprotClassificationModel | ProtT5ClassificationModel | Sequence-level multi-class classification |
| Regression | SaprotRegressionModel | ProtT5RegressionModel | Sequence-level continuous value prediction |
| Token Classification | SaprotTokenClassificationModel | ProtT5TokenClassificationModel | Residue-level classification |
| Pair Classification | SaprotPairClassificationModel | - | Classification for sequence pairs |
| Pair Regression | SaprotPairRegressionModel | - | Regression for sequence pairs |

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:53](), [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:58]()

## Model Forward Pass Flow

The following diagram illustrates the forward pass flow for a typical model in SaprotHub:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input Sequences/Structures"] --> Tokenizer["Tokenizer Encoding"]
    Tokenizer --> InputFeatures["Input Features 
    (input_ids, attention_mask)"]
    
    InputFeatures --> BiasFeature{"Structure Info?"}
    BiasFeature -- "Yes" --> AddBias["Add Structure as Bias Features"]
    BiasFeature -- "No" --> FrozenBackbone{"Frozen Backbone?"}
    AddBias --> FrozenBackbone
    
    FrozenBackbone -- "Yes" --> MeanPooling["Mean Pooling of Hidden States"]
    FrozenBackbone -- "No" --> ModelForward["Full Model Forward Pass"]
    
    MeanPooling --> TaskHead["Task-specific Head"]
    ModelForward --> TaskHead
    
    TaskHead --> OutputLogits["Output Logits/Values"]
    OutputLogits --> LossFunction["Loss Function"]
    
    LossFunction --> UpdateMetrics["Update Metrics"]
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:257-325](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:36-60](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:39-63](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:48-70]()

## Learning Rate Schedulers

SaprotHub implements several learning rate schedulers to optimize the training process:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "LR Schedulers"
        Constant["ConstantLRScheduler
        (fixed learning rate)"]
        
        Cosine["CosineAnnealingLRScheduler
        (warmup + cosine decay)"]
        
        ESM2["Esm2LRScheduler
        (warmup + plateau + linear decay)"]
    end
    
    Constant --> Training["Model Training"]
    Cosine --> Training
    ESM2 --> Training
```

The learning rate schedulers are essential components of the training process:

1. **ConstantLRScheduler**: Maintains a fixed learning rate throughout training
2. **CosineAnnealingLRScheduler**: Includes a warmup phase followed by cosine decay to final learning rate
3. **Esm2LRScheduler**: Implements ESM2's learning rate schedule with warmup, plateau, and linear decay phases

Sources: [saprot/utils/lr_scheduler.py:6-186](), [saprot/model/abstract_model.py:378-400]()

## Training Integration

The model architecture is integrated into the training pipeline through the following process:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Config["Configuration Loading"] --> ModelInit["Model Initialization"]
    ModelInit --> DatasetInit["Dataset Initialization"]
    DatasetInit --> TrainerInit["Trainer Initialization"]
    
    TrainerInit --> Training["Model Training"]
    Training --> BestModel["Load Best Model"]
    BestModel --> Testing["Model Testing"]
    
    subgraph "LoRA Workflow"
        LoRACheck{"Using LoRA?"}
        LoadLoRA["Load LoRA Adapters"]
        ConfigureLoRA["Configure LoRA Params"]
    end
    
    BestModel --> LoRACheck
    LoRACheck -- "Yes" --> ConfigureLoRA
    ConfigureLoRA --> LoadLoRA
    LoadLoRA --> Testing
    LoRACheck -- "No" --> Testing
```

Sources: [saprot/scripts/training.py:20-103]()

## Conclusion

SaprotHub's model architecture provides a flexible and extensible framework for working with protein language models. The modular design with an abstract base class and specialized implementations for different tasks allows for easy extension and customization. The integration of LoRA enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning, making it possible to adapt large protein language models to specific tasks with limited computational resources.

The architecture supports both ESM-based and T5-based protein language models, each with their own specialized implementations for different prediction tasks. This flexibility, combined with configurable learning rate schedules and training integration, makes SaprotHub a powerful tool for protein engineering and analysis.

For more details on specific model types and their applications, see [SaProt Base Model](#3.1) and [ProtT5 Models](#3.2).

# Page: SaProt Base Model

# SaProt Base Model

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [saprot/model/abstract_model.py](saprot/model/abstract_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/base.py](saprot/model/saprot/base.py)
- [saprot/scripts/training.py](saprot/scripts/training.py)
- [saprot/utils/lr_scheduler.py](saprot/utils/lr_scheduler.py)

</details>



This document details the SaProt Base Model, which serves as the foundational architecture for protein language model implementations in the SaprotHub framework. The SaProt Base Model provides a standardized interface for initializing, configuring, and training protein language models, with specific focus on efficient fine-tuning capabilities through Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA).

For information about task-specific model implementations that extend this base model, see [Model Types and Prediction Tasks](#3.3).

## 1. Architecture Overview

The SaProt Base Model inherits from the AbstractModel class, establishing a consistent interface for protein language model implementations in SaprotHub. It acts as an intermediary layer that handles model initialization, task-specific adaptations, and integration of efficient fine-tuning techniques.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class AbstractModel {
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +test_step()
        +load_checkpoint()
        +save_checkpoint()
    }
    
    class SaprotBaseModel {
        +task: str
        +config_path: str
        +load_pretrained: bool
        +freeze_backbone: bool
        +gradient_checkpointing: bool
        +lora_kwargs: dict
        +initialize_model()
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
        +get_hidden_states_from_seqs()
        +add_bias_feature()
    }
    
    AbstractModel <|-- SaprotBaseModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- "SaprotClassificationModel"
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- "SaprotRegressionModel"
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- "SaprotTokenClassificationModel"
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- "SaprotPairClassificationModel"
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- "SaprotPairRegressionModel"
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:21-63](), [saprot/model/abstract_model.py:12-40]()

## 2. Initialization and Configuration

The SaprotBaseModel is designed to be highly configurable, supporting various tasks and model architectures. Its initialization process handles:

1. Task specification ('classification', 'token_classification', 'regression', 'lm', or 'base')
2. Model configuration path for loading the HuggingFace ESM model 
3. Additional configuration options such as whether to freeze backbone or enable gradient checkpointing
4. Learning rate scheduler and optimizer parameters
5. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) configuration for efficient fine-tuning

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Init["SaprotBaseModel.__init__"] --> TaskCheck["Assert valid task type"]
    TaskCheck --> SuperInit["Call AbstractModel.__init__"]
    SuperInit --> CheckLora["Check for LoRA configuration"]
    CheckLora -->|"LoRA config present"| DisableFreeze["Disable backbone freezing"]
    DisableFreeze --> InitLora["Initialize LoRA (_init_lora)"]
    InitLora --> InitOptimizers["Initialize optimizers"]
    CheckLora -->|"No LoRA config"| SetupMetrics["Setup validation metrics"]
    
    InitModel["initialize_model"] --> InitTokenizer["Initialize tokenizer"]
    InitTokenizer --> LoadConfig["Load model configuration"]
    LoadConfig --> TaskSwitch{"Task type?"}
    
    TaskSwitch -->|"classification"| ClassModel["Initialize classification model"]
    TaskSwitch -->|"token_classification"| TokenModel["Initialize token classification model"]
    TaskSwitch -->|"regression"| RegModel["Initialize regression model"]
    TaskSwitch -->|"lm"| LMModel["Initialize masked LM model"]
    TaskSwitch -->|"base"| BaseModel["Initialize base model"]
    
    ClassModel --> CheckFreeze["Check if backbone should be frozen"]
    TokenModel --> CheckFreeze
    RegModel --> CheckFreeze
    LMModel --> CheckFreeze
    BaseModel --> CheckFreeze
    
    CheckFreeze -->|"True"| FreezeParams["Freeze ESM backbone parameters"]
    CheckFreeze -->|"False"| ModelReady["Model initialization complete"]
    FreezeParams --> ModelReady
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:26-71](), [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:175-252]()

### 2.1 Supported Task Types

The SaprotBaseModel supports multiple task types, each corresponding to a specific model architecture:

| Task Type | Model Class | Description | Use Case |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|----------|
| `classification` | `AutoModelForSequenceClassification` | Predicts discrete labels for proteins | Protein function prediction, localization, etc. |
| `token_classification` | `AutoModelForTokenClassification` | Predicts labels for each amino acid | Secondary structure prediction, residue property prediction |
| `regression` | `AutoModelForSequenceClassification` (num_labels=1) | Predicts continuous values | Stability prediction, binding affinity, etc. |
| `lm` | `AutoModelForMaskedLM` | Masked language modeling task | Pretraining, mutation effect prediction |
| `base` | `AutoModelForMaskedLM` (modified) | Base representation without prediction heads | Feature extraction for custom downstream tasks |

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:175-233]()

## 3. LoRA Integration

One of the key features of the SaprotBaseModel is its integration with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique. LoRA allows for fine-tuning large protein language models with significantly fewer trainable parameters, reducing memory requirements and training time.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InitLora["_init_lora"] --> ImportPeft["Import PEFT modules"]
    ImportPeft --> GetTrainable["Get is_trainable flag"]
    GetTrainable --> ConfigCheck["Check config_list length"]
    
    ConfigCheck --> LoRALoop["For each LoRA model (i=0 to num_lora-1)"]
    
    LoRALoop --> AdapterName["Set adapter name"]
    AdapterName --> ConfigListCheck{"i < len(config_list)?"}
    
    ConfigListCheck -->|"Yes"| LoadPretrained["Load pre-trained LoRA weights"]
    ConfigListCheck -->|"No"| CreateNewLoRA["Initialize new LoRA adapter"]
    
    LoadPretrained --> FirstAdapter{"i == 0?"}
    FirstAdapter -->|"Yes"| InitPEFT["Initialize PEFT model"]
    FirstAdapter -->|"No"| LoadAdapter["Load adapter to existing model"]
    
    CreateNewLoRA --> SetupConfig["Setup LoRA configuration"]
    SetupConfig --> FirstNewAdapter{"i == 0?"}
    FirstNewAdapter -->|"Yes"| GetPeftModel["Initialize PEFT model"]
    FirstNewAdapter -->|"No"| AddAdapter["Add adapter to existing model"]
    
    InitPEFT --> NextIter["Next iteration"]
    LoadAdapter --> NextIter
    GetPeftModel --> NextIter
    AddAdapter --> NextIter
    
    NextIter --> CheckMultiLoRA{"num_lora > 1?"}
    CheckMultiLoRA -->|"Yes"| SetupEnsemble["Setup LoRA ensemble forward function"]
    CheckMultiLoRA -->|"No"| LoraComplete["LoRA initialization complete"]
    SetupEnsemble --> LoraComplete
    
    LoraComplete --> InitOptimizers["Initialize optimizers with trainable parameters"]
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:74-173]()

### 3.1 LoRA Configuration Options

The LoRA integration supports the following key configuration parameters:

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `num_lora` | Number of LoRA adapters to use | Required |
| `config_list` | List of pre-trained LoRA configurations to load | `[]` |
| `is_trainable` | Whether the LoRA adapters should be trainable | `False` |
| `r` | Rank of the LoRA adaptation matrices | `8` |
| `lora_dropout` | Dropout probability for LoRA layers | `0.0` |
| `lora_alpha` | Scaling factor for LoRA | `16` |
| `target_modules` | Which modules to apply LoRA to | `["query", "key", "value", "intermediate.dense", "output.dense"]` |

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:105-113]()

### 3.2 Multi-LoRA Ensemble

The SaprotBaseModel supports ensembling multiple LoRA adapters. When multiple LoRA adapters are used, the model operates in inference mode only, averaging predictions from all adapters:

- For classification tasks: Final predictions are determined by voting among all LoRA models
- For regression tasks: Final predictions are the average of predictions from all LoRA models

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:124-167]()

## 4. Hidden State Extraction

The SaprotBaseModel provides methods to extract hidden representations from protein sequences, which are essential for many downstream tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input"] -->|"Dictionary"| DictMethod["get_hidden_states_from_dict"]
    Input -->|"Sequences"| SeqMethod["get_hidden_states_from_seqs"]
    
    DictMethod --> SetOutput["Set output_hidden_states=True"]
    SetOutput --> ForwardPass["Forward pass through model"]
    ForwardPass --> FindEOS["Find EOS token indices"]
    FindEOS --> GetLastLayer["Get hidden states from last layer"]
    GetLastLayer --> ProcessReps["Process representations"]
    
    SeqMethod --> Tokenize["Tokenize sequences"]
    Tokenize --> MoveToDevice["Move tensors to device"]
    MoveToDevice --> SeqForward["Forward pass through model"]
    SeqForward --> SeqFindEOS["Find EOS token indices"]
    SeqFindEOS --> SeqGetLastLayer["Get hidden states from last layer"]
    SeqGetLastLayer --> SeqProcessReps["Process representations"]
    
    ProcessReps --> ReductionCheck{"reduction?"}
    ReductionCheck -->|"mean"| MeanPool["Average over sequence length"]
    ReductionCheck -->|"None"| KeepAll["Keep full sequence representation"]
    MeanPool --> ReturnReps["Return representations"]
    KeepAll --> ReturnReps
    
    SeqProcessReps --> SeqReductionCheck{"reduction?"}
    SeqReductionCheck -->|"mean"| SeqMeanPool["Average over sequence length"]
    SeqReductionCheck -->|"None"| SeqKeepAll["Keep full sequence representation"]
    SeqMeanPool --> SeqReturnReps["Return representations"]
    SeqKeepAll --> SeqReturnReps
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:257-325]()

## 5. Structure-Aware Features

The SaprotBaseModel can incorporate structural information through the `add_bias_feature` method. This method adds structure information as biases to attention maps, similar to how the Evoformer architecture works:

```python
def add_bias_feature(self, inputs, coords: List[Dict]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Add structure information as biases to attention map. This function is used to add structure information
    to the model as Evoformer does.
    """
    inputs["pair_feature"] = batch_coords2feature(coords, self.model.device)
    return inputs
```

This enables structure-aware protein language modeling, where the model can leverage both sequence and structural information for improved predictions.

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:327-340]()

## 6. Training and Optimization

The SaprotBaseModel leverages PyTorch Lightning for training, with support for various optimization strategies. The model uses different learning rate schedulers to control the learning process during training.

### 6.1 Learning Rate Schedulers

The SaprotBaseModel supports several learning rate schedulers:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    LRSchedulers["Learning Rate Schedulers"] --> Constant["ConstantLRScheduler"]
    LRSchedulers --> Cosine["CosineAnnealingLRScheduler"]
    LRSchedulers --> ESM2["Esm2LRScheduler"]
    
    Constant --> ConstDesc["Maintains fixed learning rate"]
    
    Cosine --> WarmupPhase["Warmup phase: linear increase"]
    WarmupPhase --> AnealingPhase["Annealing phase: cosine decay"]
    
    ESM2 --> ESM2Warmup["Warmup phase: linear increase"]
    ESM2Warmup --> ESM2Plateau["Plateau phase: constant LR"]
    ESM2Plateau --> ESM2Decay["Decay phase: linear decrease"]
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/lr_scheduler.py:6-187](), [saprot/model/abstract_model.py:378-400]()

### 6.2 Optimizer Configuration

The model uses the AdamW optimizer by default, with different weight decay settings for different parameter groups:

- No weight decay for layer normalization weights and biases
- Standard weight decay for all other parameters

This approach helps prevent overfitting while still allowing certain critical parameters to adapt properly.

Sources: [saprot/model/abstract_model.py:378-400]()

## 7. Model Saving and Loading

The SaprotBaseModel provides custom methods for saving and loading model checkpoints, with special handling for LoRA models.

### 7.1 Checkpoint Saving

For standard models, the checkpoint contains the model weights and optionally the optimizer and scheduler states. For LoRA models, the model is saved using the PEFT library's `save_pretrained` method, which preserves the LoRA adaptation parameters.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Save["save_checkpoint"] --> LoraCheck{"Has LoRA config?"}
    LoraCheck -->|"No"| SuperSave["Call AbstractModel.save_checkpoint"]
    LoraCheck -->|"Yes"| DeepSpeedCheck{"Using DeepSpeed?"}
    DeepSpeedCheck -->|"Yes"| AdjustPath["Adjust save path"]
    DeepSpeedCheck -->|"No"| SaveLoRA["Use model.save_pretrained"]
    AdjustPath --> SaveLoRA
```

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:342-358](), [saprot/model/abstract_model.py:267-296]()

### 7.2 Evaluation and Metrics

The SaprotBaseModel provides methods for evaluating model performance and displaying metrics during training and testing. It supports different metrics based on the task type:

| Task Type | Primary Metrics |
|-----------|----------------|
| Classification | Accuracy (Acc), Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) |
| Regression | Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), R², Spearman correlation, Pearson correlation |
| Token Classification | Accuracy, MCC (for binary), F1 score |

For interactive environments like Google Colab, the model can plot validation metric curves to help users monitor training progress and detect overfitting.

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/base.py:359-452]()

## Summary

The SaprotBaseModel serves as the foundation for all protein language model implementations in SaprotHub. It provides a flexible and configurable architecture that supports various tasks and efficient fine-tuning through LoRA. Key features include:

1. Support for different task types (classification, regression, token classification)
2. Integration with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
3. Multi-adapter ensembling for improved model performance
4. Methods for extracting hidden representations from protein sequences
5. Structure-aware modeling capabilities through attention biases
6. Comprehensive training and evaluation utilities

This base model is extended by task-specific models to provide specialized functionality for different protein prediction tasks.

---

# Page: ProtT5 Models

# ProtT5 Models

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [saprot/model/protT5/base.py](saprot/model/protT5/base.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py)

</details>



This page documents the ProtT5 models in SaprotHub, focusing on their architecture, implementation, and usage. ProtT5 models are based on the T5 encoder transformer architecture, specifically designed for protein sequence analysis tasks. For information about SaProt models, see [SaProt Base Model](#3.1).

## Overview

ProtT5 models use transformer-based neural networks to learn protein sequence representations. The models leverage the T5 encoder architecture and can be fine-tuned for various downstream tasks using parameter-efficient techniques like LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation).

```mermaid
classDiagram
    AbstractModel <|-- ProtT5BaseModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5ClassificationModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5RegressionModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5TokenClassificationModel
    
    class AbstractModel {
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +test_step()
        +load_checkpoint()
        +save_checkpoint()
    }
    
    class ProtT5BaseModel {
        +task: str
        +config_path: str
        +freeze_backbone: bool
        +gradient_checkpointing: bool
        +lora_kwargs: dict
        +initialize_model()
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
        +add_bias_feature()
        +save_checkpoint()
    }
    
    class ProtT5ClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +initialize_metrics()
    }
    
    class ProtT5RegressionModel {
        +test_result_path: str
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +initialize_metrics()
    }
    
    class ProtT5TokenClassificationModel {
        +num_labels: int
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +initialize_metrics()
        +compute_mcc()
    }
```

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:27-393](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:10-106](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:9-126](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:10-166]()

## ProtT5BaseModel

`ProtT5BaseModel` serves as the foundation for all ProtT5 models in SaprotHub. It cannot be used directly but provides essential functionality for downstream task-specific models.

### Initialization

The base model is initialized with several key parameters:

```python
def __init__(self,
             task: str,
             config_path: str,
             extra_config: dict = None,
             load_pretrained: bool = False,
             freeze_backbone: bool = False,
             gradient_checkpointing: bool = False,
             lora_kwargs: dict = None,
             **kwargs):
```

- `task`: Specifies the task type ('classification', 'token_classification', 'regression', 'lm', or 'base')
- `config_path`: Path to the HuggingFace configuration file for the T5 model
- `extra_config`: Additional configuration parameters
- `load_pretrained`: Whether to load pretrained weights
- `freeze_backbone`: Whether to freeze the encoder backbone
- `gradient_checkpointing`: Whether to enable gradient checkpointing (for memory efficiency)
- `lora_kwargs`: Configuration for LoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:27-76]()

### Model Initialization

The model initialization process:

1. Sets up the T5 tokenizer based on the provided config path
2. Initializes the appropriate model based on the task type
3. Applies additional configuration as needed

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["initialize_model()"] --> LoadTokenizer["Load T5Tokenizer"]
    LoadTokenizer --> LoadConfig["Load T5Config"]
    LoadConfig --> TaskCheck{"Task Type?"}
    
    TaskCheck -->|"classification"| CLSModel["T5ForSequenceClassification"]
    TaskCheck -->|"token_classification"| TokenModel["T5ForTokenClassification"]
    TaskCheck -->|"regression"| RegModel["T5ForSequenceClassification\nwith num_labels=1"]
    
    CLSModel --> InitClassifier["Initialize classifier head"]
    TokenModel --> InitClassifier
    RegModel --> InitClassifier
    
    subgraph "Classifier Head Structure"
        InitClassifier --> Linear1["Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size)"]
        Linear1 --> ReLU["ReLU activation"]
        ReLU --> Linear2["Linear(hidden_size, num_labels)"]
    end
```

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:182-260]()

### LoRA Integration

The base model supports LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning:

1. Configures LoRA adapters for specific modules (attention components)
2. Supports multiple LoRA adapters for ensemble prediction
3. Handles adapter saving and loading

Key LoRA parameters:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| r | 8 | LoRA rank (lower values = fewer parameters) |
| lora_dropout | 0.0 | Dropout rate for LoRA layers |
| lora_alpha | 16 | LoRA scaling factor |

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:79-181]()

### Feature Extraction

The model provides methods to extract features from protein sequences:

```python
def get_hidden_states_from_dict(self, inputs: dict, reduction: str = None) -> list:
```

This method processes input token IDs and attention masks to extract hidden representations from the model. If `reduction="mean"`, it averages the representations across the sequence length.

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:264-296]()

### Structural Information Integration

The model can incorporate structural information through:

```python
def add_bias_feature(self, inputs, coords: List[Dict]) -> torch.Tensor:
```

This method adds structure information as biases to attention maps, similar to how Evoformer works. It uses backbone atom coordinates (N, CA, C, O) to compute pair features.

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:334-347]()

## Task-Specific Models

SaprotHub provides three specialized ProtT5 models for different tasks:

### 1. ProtT5ClassificationModel

For sequence-level classification tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Protein Sequence"] --> Tokenize["T5 Tokenizer"]
    Tokenize --> T5Encoder["T5 Encoder"]
    T5Encoder --> PoolMean["Mean Pooling"]
    PoolMean --> Classifier["Classification Head"]
    Classifier --> Output["Class Probabilities"]
```

Key features:
- Takes `num_labels` to specify the number of classes
- Uses mean pooling to aggregate sequence representations
- Uses cross-entropy loss
- Tracks accuracy metrics

Implementation details:
- The classifier head consists of two linear layers with a ReLU activation
- Supports optional structure-aware features through the `coords` parameter

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:10-106]()

### 2. ProtT5RegressionModel

For sequence-level regression tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Protein Sequence"] --> Tokenize["T5 Tokenizer"]
    Tokenize --> T5Encoder["T5 Encoder"]
    T5Encoder --> PoolMean["Mean Pooling"]
    PoolMean --> Regressor["Regression Head"]
    Regressor --> Output["Continuous Value"]
```

Key features:
- Uses mean squared error loss
- Tracks multiple metrics: MSE, Spearman correlation, R², Pearson correlation
- Can save test results to a specified path

The model uses the same architecture as the classification model but with a single output unit and different loss function and metrics.

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:9-126]()

### 3. ProtT5TokenClassificationModel

For residue-level (token-level) classification tasks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Protein Sequence"] --> Tokenize["T5 Tokenizer"]
    Tokenize --> T5Encoder["T5 Encoder"]
    T5Encoder --> PerToken["Per-Token Representations"]
    PerToken --> Classifier["Token Classification Head"]
    Classifier --> Output["Per-Residue Classifications"]
```

Key features:
- Predicts a class for each amino acid (token) in the sequence
- Uses cross-entropy loss (ignoring padding tokens)
- Computes Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) in addition to accuracy
- Supports structure-aware features through the `coords` parameter

Unlike the sequence-level models, this model doesn't perform pooling, preserving token-level representations for prediction.

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:10-166]()

## Forward Pass Data Flow

The following diagram illustrates the data flow during a forward pass through a ProtT5 model:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    InputDict["Input Dictionary\n(input_ids, attention_mask)"] --> StructCheck{"Has Structure\nCoordinates?"}
    
    StructCheck -->|"Yes"| AddBias["Add Structural Bias Features"]
    StructCheck -->|"No"| FreezeCheck
    
    AddBias --> FreezeCheck{"Backbone\nFrozen?"}
    
    FreezeCheck -->|"Yes"| GetHidden["Get Hidden States\nwith Reduction"]
    FreezeCheck -->|"No"| ModelForward["Model Forward Pass"]
    
    GetHidden --> ClassifierDrop["Classifier Dropout"]
    ClassifierDrop --> ClassifierDense["Classifier Dense Layer"]
    ClassifierDense --> Tanh["Tanh Activation"]
    Tanh --> ClassifierDrop2["Classifier Dropout"]
    ClassifierDrop2 --> OutProj["Output Projection"]
    
    ModelForward --> LastHidden["Extract Last Hidden State"]
    LastHidden --> TaskCheck{"Task Type?"}
    
    TaskCheck -->|"Classification\nRegression"| MeanPool["Mean Pooling"]
    TaskCheck -->|"Token\nClassification"| NoPool["No Pooling"]
    
    MeanPool --> ClassHead["Classification/Regression Head"]
    NoPool --> TokenHead["Token Classification Head"]
    
    ClassHead --> Logits["Output Logits"]
    TokenHead --> Logits
    OutProj --> Logits
```

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:36-60](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:39-63](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:48-70]()

## Integration with SaprotHub

ProtT5 models are registered through the model interface system and can be accessed through:

1. The main SaprotHub notebook interface
2. The specialized ColabProtT5 interface

The models use the `@register_model` decorator to make them available to the SaprotHub system.

## Usage Considerations

When using ProtT5 models, consider the following:

| Aspect | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| Memory Usage | ProtT5 models can be large; consider using gradient checkpointing or LoRA for efficiency |
| Tokenization | Uses T5 tokenizer which handles amino acid sequences differently than language models |
| Task Selection | Choose the appropriate model (Classification, Regression, TokenClassification) based on task |
| Structural Data | Consider adding structural information using the `add_bias_feature` method for potentially improved performance |
| Fine-tuning | LoRA adapters provide parameter-efficient fine-tuning with fewer resources |

## Metrics Visualization

ProtT5 models include built-in visualization of validation metrics using matplotlib through Google Colab widgets. This allows real-time monitoring of training progress.

The `plot_valid_metrics_curve` method creates visualizations for all tracked metrics over training steps.

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:366-392]()

# Page: Model Types and Prediction Tasks

# Model Types and Prediction Tasks

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [saprot/model/protT5/base.py](saprot/model/protT5/base.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py)
- [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py](saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_regression_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_regression_model.py)
- [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_token_classification_model.py](saprot/model/saprot/saprot_token_classification_model.py)

</details>



This page provides a technical overview of the various model types available in SaprotHub and the prediction tasks they support. It explains the architecture of each model type, their inheritance relationships, supported tasks, and how to choose the appropriate model for different protein-related predictions.

## Model Type Overview

The SaprotHub system implements two main families of protein language models:

1. **SaProt-based models**: Built on ESM protein language models
2. **ProtT5-based models**: Built on the T5 transformer architecture optimized for proteins

Both model families inherit from an abstract base class and are further specialized for different prediction tasks.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    AbstractModel <|-- SaprotBaseModel
    AbstractModel <|-- ProtT5BaseModel
    
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotRegressionModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotTokenClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairClassificationModel
    SaprotBaseModel <|-- SaprotPairRegressionModel
    
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5ClassificationModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5RegressionModel
    ProtT5BaseModel <|-- ProtT5TokenClassificationModel
    
    class AbstractModel {
        +initialize_model()
        +forward()
        +loss_func()
        +training_step()
        +validation_step()
        +test_step()
    }
    
    class SaprotBaseModel {
        +task: str
        +config_path: str
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
    }
    
    class ProtT5BaseModel {
        +task: str
        +config_path: str
        +_init_lora()
        +get_hidden_states_from_dict()
    }
```

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:27-393](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py:10-82](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_regression_model.py:9-109](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_token_classification_model.py:10-139](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model.py:11-94](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model.py:11-87](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:10-106](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:9-126](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:10-166]()

## SaProt Models

SaProt models are based on Facebook's ESM protein language models. These models use a transformer-based architecture pre-trained on large protein sequence datasets. SaprotHub provides the following specialized SaProt model types:

### SaprotClassificationModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts discrete class labels for entire protein sequences
- **Architecture**: ESM backbone with a classification head
- **Key components**:
  - Classification head: `torch.nn.Linear(hidden_size, num_labels)`
  - Loss function: Cross-entropy
  - Primary metric: Accuracy

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_classification_model.py:10-82]()

### SaprotRegressionModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts continuous values for entire protein sequences
- **Architecture**: ESM backbone with a regression head
- **Key components**:
  - Regression head: `torch.nn.Linear(hidden_size, 1)`
  - Loss function: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
  - Primary metrics: MSE, Spearman correlation, R²-score, Pearson correlation

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_regression_model.py:9-109]()

### SaprotTokenClassificationModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts labels for each amino acid (token) in a sequence
- **Architecture**: ESM backbone with a token classification head
- **Key components**:
  - Token classification head that outputs logits for each token
  - Loss function: Cross-entropy with support for ignoring certain indices
  - Primary metrics: Accuracy, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_token_classification_model.py:10-139]()

### SaprotPairClassificationModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts discrete class labels for protein pairs
- **Architecture**: ESM backbone that processes two sequences independently, then concatenates embeddings
- **Key components**:
  - Pair classifier: `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(hidden_size*2, hidden_size*2), ReLU(), Linear(hidden_size*2, num_labels))`
  - Loss function: Cross-entropy
  - Primary metric: Accuracy

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model.py:11-94]()

### SaprotPairRegressionModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts continuous values for protein pairs
- **Architecture**: Similar to pair classification but with a regression output
- **Key components**:
  - Pair regression head: `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(hidden_size*2, hidden_size*2), ReLU(), Linear(hidden_size*2, 1))`
  - Loss function: MSE
  - Primary metrics: MSE, Spearman correlation, R²-score, Pearson correlation

Sources: [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model.py:11-87]()

## ProtT5 Models

ProtT5 models are based on the T5 (Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer) architecture adapted for protein sequences. SaprotHub provides the following specialized ProtT5 model types:

### ProtT5ClassificationModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts discrete class labels for entire protein sequences
- **Architecture**: T5 encoder with a classification head
- **Key components**:
  - Classification head: `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size), ReLU(), Linear(hidden_size, num_labels))`
  - Loss function: Cross-entropy
  - Primary metric: Accuracy

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:10-106]()

### ProtT5RegressionModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts continuous values for entire protein sequences
- **Architecture**: T5 encoder with a regression head
- **Key components**:
  - Regression head: `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size), ReLU(), Linear(hidden_size, 1))`
  - Loss function: MSE
  - Primary metrics: MSE, Spearman correlation, R²-score, Pearson correlation

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:9-126]()

### ProtT5TokenClassificationModel

- **Purpose**: Predicts labels for each amino acid in a sequence
- **Architecture**: T5 encoder with a token classification head
- **Key components**:
  - Token classification head: `torch.nn.Sequential(Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size), ReLU(), Linear(hidden_size, num_labels))`
  - Loss function: Cross-entropy with support for ignoring padding tokens
  - Primary metrics: Accuracy, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:10-166]()

## Prediction Tasks

SaprotHub models are designed to support various protein-related prediction tasks. These tasks can be categorized based on their input-output characteristics.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Protein["Protein Sequence Input"] --> SeqTasks["Sequence-Level Tasks"]
    Protein --> ResTasks["Residue-Level Tasks"]
    Protein --> PairTasks["Protein Pair Tasks"]
    
    SeqTasks --> SeqCls["Classification Tasks"]
    SeqTasks --> SeqReg["Regression Tasks"]
    
    ResTasks --> TokenCls["Token Classification Tasks"]
    
    PairTasks --> PairCls["Pair Classification Tasks"]
    PairTasks --> PairReg["Pair Regression Tasks"]
    
    SeqCls --> ClsExamples["Function Prediction,
                         Subcellular Localization"]
    SeqReg --> RegExamples["Stability Prediction,
                        Binding Affinity"]
    TokenCls --> TokenExamples["Secondary Structure,
                           Solvent Accessibility"]
    PairCls --> PairClsExamples["Protein-Protein
                           Interaction Prediction"]
    PairReg --> PairRegExamples["Binding Affinity
                           Between Proteins"]
```

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:10-106](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_regression_model.py:9-126](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_token_classification_model.py:10-166](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model.py:11-94](), [saprot/model/saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model.py:11-87]()

### Sequence-Level Tasks

#### Classification Tasks

Sequence classification tasks involve predicting discrete labels for an entire protein sequence. Examples include:

- Protein function prediction
- Subcellular localization
- Thermostability classification
- Enzyme/non-enzyme classification

The model outputs logits (one per possible class), which are converted to class probabilities via softmax.

Models supporting this task:
- `SaprotClassificationModel`
- `ProtT5ClassificationModel`

#### Regression Tasks

Sequence regression tasks involve predicting continuous values for an entire protein sequence. Examples include:

- Protein stability (ΔG)
- Binding affinity (Kd)
- Solubility
- Fitness scores

The model outputs a single continuous value for each protein.

Models supporting this task:
- `SaprotRegressionModel`
- `ProtT5RegressionModel`

### Residue-Level Tasks

Token classification tasks predict properties for each amino acid in a protein sequence. Examples include:

- Secondary structure prediction (helix, sheet, coil)
- Solvent accessibility
- Disorder prediction
- B-factor prediction
- Contact prediction

The model outputs logits for each amino acid in the sequence.

Models supporting this task:
- `SaprotTokenClassificationModel`
- `ProtT5TokenClassificationModel`

### Protein Pair Tasks

#### Pair Classification Tasks

Pair classification tasks predict discrete labels for pairs of proteins. Examples include:

- Protein-protein interaction prediction (binary)
- Antigen-antibody binding prediction
- Complex formation prediction

The model outputs logits for the protein pair.

Models supporting this task:
- `SaprotPairClassificationModel`

#### Pair Regression Tasks

Pair regression tasks predict continuous values for protein pairs. Examples include:

- Binding affinity between proteins
- Interaction energy scores
- Interface stability

The model outputs a single continuous value for the protein pair.

Models supporting this task:
- `SaprotPairRegressionModel`

## Model-Task Compatibility Matrix

The following table shows which model types support which prediction tasks:

| Task Type | SaProt Models | ProtT5 Models |
|-----------|---------------|---------------|
| Classification | SaprotClassificationModel | ProtT5ClassificationModel |
| Regression | SaprotRegressionModel | ProtT5RegressionModel |
| Token Classification | SaprotTokenClassificationModel | ProtT5TokenClassificationModel |
| Pair Classification | SaprotPairClassificationModel | - |
| Pair Regression | SaprotPairRegressionModel | - |

Sources: All model files listed above

## Model Selection Guide

When choosing a model for your protein prediction task, consider the following factors:

### 1. Task Type

First, identify the type of prediction task:
- For whole-protein classification → Use Classification models
- For whole-protein continuous values → Use Regression models
- For per-residue predictions → Use Token Classification models
- For protein pair predictions → Use Pair models (SaProt only)

### 2. Model Family Choice

Choose between SaProt-based and ProtT5-based models:

- **SaProt models (ESM-based)**:
  - Better for evolutionary aspects of proteins
  - Supports all task types including pair tasks
  - Larger model sizes available
  - Strong performance on diverse protein tasks

- **ProtT5 models**:
  - Better handling of longer sequences
  - Efficient encoder-only architecture
  - Good performance on sequence-level and token-level tasks
  - Does not natively support pair tasks

### 3. Performance vs. Computational Resources

- Larger models generally achieve better performance but require more computational resources
- Consider using LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) for efficient fine-tuning with limited resources
- Both model families support freezing the backbone and training only classification/regression heads

### 4. Structure Awareness

Both model families can incorporate structural information when available:
- Via the `add_bias_feature` method to enhance predictions with structural context
- Structure-aware sequences can be processed using the normal sequence pathways

## Implementation Details

When implementing models, note that all model types register themselves through the `register_model` decorator, allowing them to be dynamically loaded based on configuration.

Each model implements standard methods:
- `initialize_model()`: Sets up the model architecture
- `forward()`: Defines the forward pass computation
- `loss_func()`: Specifies the loss function and metrics updates
- `initialize_metrics()`: Sets up performance metrics for the model

All models support LoRA for efficient fine-tuning through the `_init_lora()` method defined in the base classes.

Sources: [saprot/model/protT5/base.py:27-393](), [saprot/model/protT5/protT5_classification_model.py:10-106]()

# Data Processing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/Huggingface_ID.png](Figure/Huggingface_ID.png)
- [Figure/Runtime.png](Figure/Runtime.png)
- [Figure/Switch_Runtime.png](Figure/Switch_Runtime.png)
- [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py](saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py)
- [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_regression_dataset.py](saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_regression_dataset.py)
- [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py](saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py)
- [saprot/utils/construct_lmdb.py](saprot/utils/construct_lmdb.py)

</details>



This document explains how protein data is processed, transformed, and stored for model training in SaprotHub. It covers the end-to-end data processing pipeline, from input formats to the creation of model-ready batches.

For information on datasets and data formats, see [Datasets and Data Formats](#4.1). For details on training the models with this processed data, see [Training Pipeline](#5).

## Data Processing Overview

SaprotHub processes various types of protein data (amino acid sequences, structure-aware sequences, etc.) into formats suitable for protein language models. The data processing pipeline involves several key steps:

1. **Input Data Reading**: Reading data from CSV files containing sequences, labels, and metadata
2. **Data Transformation**: Processing data based on task type (classification, regression, token classification)
3. **LMDB Construction**: Storing processed data in LMDB (Lightning Memory-Mapped Database) format
4. **Dataset Creation**: Instantiating task-specific dataset classes that extend the base `LMDBDataset`
5. **Batch Preparation**: Tokenizing sequences and preparing batches for model training

### Data Processing Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Input"
        input["CSV Files"] --> |"read_csv"| df["DataFrame"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        df --> |"task_type"| process["Process by Task"]
        process --> |"classification"| class["Process Single Sequence\n+ Class Label"]
        process --> |"regression"| reg["Process Single Sequence\n+ Fitness Value"]
        process --> |"token_classification"| token["Process Sequence\n+ Token-Level Labels"]
        process --> |"pair_classification\npair_regression"| pair["Process Sequence Pairs\n+ Labels"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Storage"
        class --> convert["Convert to JSON"]
        reg --> convert
        token --> convert
        pair --> convert
        convert --> lmdb["LMDB Dataset Construction\n(dump_lmdb)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Classes"
        lmdb --> datasets["LMDBDataset"]
        datasets --> protT5class["ProtT5ClassificationDataset"]
        datasets --> protT5reg["ProtT5RegressionDataset"] 
        datasets --> protT5token["ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Training"
        protT5class --> collate["collate_fn()"]
        protT5reg --> collate
        protT5token --> collate
        collate --> tokenize["Tokenization + Padding"]
        tokenize --> batch["Model-Ready Batches"]
    end
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/construct_lmdb.py](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_regression_dataset.py](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py]()

## Input Data Formats

SaprotHub accepts protein data organized in CSV files with specific structure depending on the task type.

### CSV File Structure by Task Type

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class BaseCSV {
        stage (train/valid/test)
    }
    
    class ClassificationCSV {
        sequence
        label (integer)
        stage
    }
    
    class RegressionCSV {
        sequence
        fitness (float)
        stage
    }
    
    class TokenClassificationCSV {
        sequence
        label (comma-separated integers)
        stage
    }
    
    class PairCSV {
        sequence_1
        sequence_2
        label
        stage
        name_1 (optional)
        name_2 (optional)
        chain_1 (optional)
        chain_2 (optional)
    }
    
    BaseCSV <|-- ClassificationCSV
    BaseCSV <|-- RegressionCSV
    BaseCSV <|-- TokenClassificationCSV
    BaseCSV <|-- PairCSV
```

CSV file examples:

#### Classification Task CSV

| sequence | label | stage |
|----------|-------|-------|
| MKTVRQERLKSIVRILERSKEPVSGAQ... | 0 | train |
| GSSGSSGILQSAFHYLKHVVPIPPAV... | 1 | train |
| ... | ... | ... |
| MGLSDGEWQLVLNVWGKVEADIPGHG... | 0 | valid |
| ... | ... | ... |
| GSHMQEIVLTQSPATLSLSPGERATLSCRA... | 1 | test |

#### Token Classification Task CSV

| sequence | label | stage |
|----------|-------|-------|
| MKTVQERLK... | 0,1,0,0,1,0,1,0,0,... | train |
| ... | ... | ... |

Sources: [saprot/utils/construct_lmdb.py:21-44]()

## LMDB Dataset Construction

The `construct_lmdb` function transforms the input CSV data into LMDB format for efficient storage and retrieval during training.

### Transformation Process

1. **CSV Loading**: The function reads the CSV file and normalizes column names to lowercase
2. **Task-Specific Processing**: 
   - For token classification, converts comma-separated labels to integer lists
   - For single sequence tasks, extracts sequence, label, and stage
   - For pair tasks, extracts both sequences, labels, and metadata
3. **JSON Conversion**: Creates JSON objects containing processed data
4. **LMDB Creation**: Stores data in LMDB format organized by train/valid/test stages

```python
# LMDB construction process (simplified)
for stage in ["train", "valid", "test"]:
    tmp_dict = data_dicts[stage]
    tmp_dict["length"] = len(tmp_dict)
    lmdb_dir = f"{root_dir}/{dataset_name}/{stage}"
    dump_lmdb(tmp_dict, lmdb_dir)
```

The resulting LMDB databases are organized by stages (train, valid, test), with each stage stored in a separate directory. Within each directory, data is stored as key-value pairs where keys are indices and values are JSON-encoded data samples.

Sources: [saprot/utils/construct_lmdb.py:78-119]()

## Specialized Dataset Classes

SaprotHub provides specialized dataset classes for different tasks, all extending the base `LMDBDataset` class. These classes handle the retrieval, processing, and batching of data from LMDB storage.

### Dataset Class Hierarchy

```mermaid
classDiagram
    LMDBDataset <|-- ProtT5ClassificationDataset
    LMDBDataset <|-- ProtT5RegressionDataset
    LMDBDataset <|-- ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset
    
    class LMDBDataset {
        +__init__(lmdb_dir, db_name)
        +_get(index)
        +__getitem__(index)
        +__len__()
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class ProtT5ClassificationDataset {
        +tokenizer: T5Tokenizer
        +max_length: int
        +use_bias_feature: bool
        +preset_label: int
        +mask_struc_ratio: float
        +mask_seed: int
        +plddt_threshold: float
        +__getitem__(index)
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class ProtT5RegressionDataset {
        +tokenizer: T5Tokenizer
        +max_length: int
        +min_clip: [float, float]
        +mix_max_norm: [float, float]
        +mask_struc_ratio: float
        +plddt_threshold: float
        +__getitem__(index)
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset {
        +tokenizer: T5Tokenizer
        +max_length: int
        +__getitem__(index)
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
```

Each dataset class is registered using the `@register_dataset` decorator, which allows the system to dynamically load the appropriate dataset class based on the task type.

Sources: [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py:15-67](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_regression_dataset.py:13-80](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py:12-56]()

### Classification Dataset

The `ProtT5ClassificationDataset` handles classification tasks and supports the following key features:

- **Sequence Retrieval**: Extracts amino acid sequences from LMDB storage
- **Label Processing**: Handles class labels (integers)
- **Optional Features**:
  - `use_bias_feature`: Option to incorporate structural information
  - `preset_label`: Override stored labels with a fixed value
  - `mask_struc_ratio`: Mask a portion of structural tokens for robustness
  - `plddt_threshold`: Mask tokens with pLDDT scores below threshold

```python
# Item retrieval for classification dataset
def __getitem__(self, index):
    entry = json.loads(self._get(index))
    seq = entry['seq'][::2]  # Extract every other character
    seq = " ".join(seq)      # Add space between amino acids
    
    # Use preset label if provided, otherwise use stored label
    label = entry["label"] if self.preset_label is None else self.preset_label

    return seq, label
```

Sources: [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py:47-54]()

### Regression Dataset

The `ProtT5RegressionDataset` extends the base dataset for regression tasks with these key features:

- **Fitness Value Processing**: Handles continuous values for regression tasks
- **Value Normalization**: Optional min-max normalization of fitness values
- **Value Clipping**: Option to clip values below a threshold to a specific value

```python
# Value processing in regression dataset
if self.min_clip is not None:
    given_min, clip_value = self.min_clip
    if entry['fitness'] < given_min:
        entry['fitness'] = clip_value

if self.mix_max_norm is not None:
    min_norm, max_norm = self.mix_max_norm
    entry['fitness'] = (entry['fitness'] - min_norm) / (max_norm - min_norm)
```

Sources: [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_regression_dataset.py:56-64]()

### Token Classification Dataset

The `ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset` handles tasks where each amino acid token has a corresponding label:

- **Token-Level Labels**: Processes per-token labels for tasks like secondary structure prediction
- **Label Truncation/Padding**: Ensures labels match the max sequence length
- **Special Token Handling**: Adds padding token (0) at the end for the CLS token

```python
# Label processing for token classification
if len(entry["label"]) >= self.max_length:
    label = entry["label"][:self.max_length - 1] + [0]
else:
    label = entry["label"][:self.max_length] + [0]  
label = torch.tensor(label, dtype=torch.long)
```

Sources: [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py:30-37]()

## Batch Preparation and Tokenization

The final step in data processing is converting samples into model-ready batches, handled by each dataset's `collate_fn` method.

### Tokenization Process

1. **Sequence Preparation**: For ProtT5 models, spaces are added between amino acids
2. **Tokenization**: Sequences are tokenized using the T5Tokenizer
3. **Padding/Truncation**: Sequences are padded to the same length within a batch and truncated to `max_length`
4. **Tensor Conversion**: Converts tokenized sequences to PyTorch tensors

```python
# Tokenization in ProtT5ClassificationDataset
def collate_fn(self, batch):
    seqs, labels = tuple(zip(*batch))
    labels = torch.tensor(labels)
    labels = {"labels": labels}
    
    encoder_info = self.tokenizer.batch_encode_plus(
        seqs, return_tensors='pt', padding=True, 
        max_length=self.max_length, truncation=True
    )
    inputs = {"inputs": encoder_info}
    
    return inputs, labels
```

For token classification, additional steps are taken to ensure label sequences match the tokenized input:

```python
# Token classification specific processing
seqs = tuple(" ".join(seq) for seq in seqs)
label_ids = pad_sequences(label_ids, constant_value=0)
labels = {"labels": label_ids}
```

Sources: [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py:59-67](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py:44-56]()

## Data Processing Flow Example

To illustrate the complete data processing flow, let's follow an example of a classification task:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Input"
        csv["CSV File:<br>sequence, label, stage"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        csv --> construct["construct_lmdb()"]
        construct --> lmdb["LMDB Databases:<br>/train, /valid, /test"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Creation"
        lmdb --> dataset["ProtT5ClassificationDataset"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training"
        dataset --> getitem["__getitem__(index):<br>Get sequence and label"]
        getitem --> collate["collate_fn(batch):<br>Tokenize and batch"]
        collate --> model["Model Training"]
    end
```

1. **CSV Input**: A CSV file with protein sequences, labels, and stages is provided
2. **LMDB Construction**: `construct_lmdb` processes the CSV and creates LMDB databases
3. **Dataset Instantiation**: A `ProtT5ClassificationDataset` is created with the LMDB path
4. **Data Retrieval**: During training, `__getitem__` retrieves sequences and labels
5. **Batch Preparation**: `collate_fn` tokenizes sequences and prepares batches
6. **Model Training**: Prepared batches are fed to the model for training

Sources: [saprot/utils/construct_lmdb.py](), [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py]()

## Summary

The data processing pipeline in SaprotHub provides a flexible and efficient system for preparing protein data for model training. Key strengths include:

1. **Task Flexibility**: Handles various tasks including classification, regression, and token-level prediction
2. **Efficient Storage**: LMDB provides fast random access to large datasets
3. **Specialized Processing**: Task-specific dataset classes tailor data preparation to each need
4. **Integration with Tokenizers**: Seamless integration with transformer tokenizers
5. **Batch Optimization**: Handles variable-length sequences with proper padding and truncation

For more information on how these processed datasets are used in training, see [Training Pipeline](#5). For details on specific dataset formats, see [Datasets and Data Formats](#4.1).

This document details the dataset structures and formats used in SaprotHub for training and evaluating protein language models. Understanding these formats is essential for creating custom datasets, interpreting model inputs/outputs, and extending SaprotHub for new protein analysis tasks.

For information about how LMDB datasets are constructed for efficient storage, see [LMDB Dataset Construction](#4.2). For details on how protein structures are processed into sequence formats, see [Protein Structure Handling](#4.3).

## Dataset System Architecture

SaprotHub implements a hierarchical dataset system built on the Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB) for efficient storage and retrieval of protein data. All dataset implementations inherit from a base `LMDBDataset` class.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    LMDBDataset <|-- ProtT5ClassificationDataset
    LMDBDataset <|-- ProtT5RegressionDataset
    LMDBDataset <|-- ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset
    
    class LMDBDataset {
        +__init__(lmdb_path, **kwargs)
        +_get(key)
        +__getitem__(index)
        +__len__()
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class ProtT5ClassificationDataset {
        +tokenizer: T5Tokenizer
        +max_length: int
        +use_bias_feature: bool
        +preset_label: int
        +mask_struc_ratio: float
        +__getitem__(index)
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class ProtT5RegressionDataset {
        +tokenizer: T5Tokenizer
        +max_length: int
        +min_clip: list
        +mix_max_norm: list
        +mask_struc_ratio: float
        +__getitem__(index)
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset {
        +tokenizer: T5Tokenizer
        +max_length: int
        +__getitem__(index)
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
```

Sources: [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_classification_dataset.py:15-46](). [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_regression_dataset.py:13-49](). [saprot/dataset/protT5/protT5_token_classification_dataset.py:12-27]().

## Data Flow in SaprotHub

The following diagram illustrates how data flows through the dataset system in SaprotHub, from input formats to model training:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Data Formats"
        AA["AA Sequence"] 
        SA["Structure-Aware Sequence"]
        PDB["PDB/CIF Structure"]

    end
    
    AA --> Process
    SA --> Process
    PDB --> Process
```
