# Page: Advanced Topics

# Advanced Topics

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py](saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py)
- [saprot/utils/module_loader.py](saprot/utils/module_loader.py)

</details>



This page covers advanced features and capabilities of the SaprotHub system that extend beyond the core functionality covered in previous sections. We explore three specialized topics: the dynamic module loading system, zero-shot mutation prediction capabilities, and search engine integration. These features are designed for users who want to leverage the full power of SaprotHub for specialized research applications.

For basic model training and usage, see [Model Architecture](#3) and [Training Pipeline](#5). For deployment options, see [Deployment Options](#6).

## 7.1 Module Loading System

SaprotHub implements a flexible dynamic module loading system that allows for runtime configuration and initialization of various components. This design enables users to select and configure different models and datasets without modifying the core codebase.

### Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Config["Configuration Dictionary"] --> ModuleLoader["Module Loader System"]
    
    ModuleLoader --> ModelLoader["Model Loader"]
    ModuleLoader --> DatasetLoader["Dataset Loader"]
    ModuleLoader --> WandbLoader["WandB Logger Loader"]
    ModuleLoader --> TrainerLoader["PyTorch Lightning Trainer Loader"]
    
    ModelLoader --> |"loads appropriate class"| Models["Model Classes"]
    DatasetLoader --> |"loads appropriate class"| Datasets["Dataset Classes"]
    
    Models --> SaprotModels["SaProt Models"]
    Models --> ProtT5Models["ProtT5 Models"]
    
    SaprotModels --> |"instantiates"| SCM["SaprotClassificationModel"]
    SaprotModels --> |"instantiates"| SRM["SaprotRegressionModel"]
    SaprotModels --> |"instantiates"| STCM["SaprotTokenClassificationModel"]
    SaprotModels --> |"instantiates"| SPCM["SaprotPairClassificationModel"]
    SaprotModels --> |"instantiates"| SPRM["SaprotPairRegressionModel"]
    
    ProtT5Models --> |"instantiates"| PCM["ProtT5ClassificationModel"]
    ProtT5Models --> |"instantiates"| PRM["ProtT5RegressionModel"]
    ProtT5Models --> |"instantiates"| PTCM["ProtT5TokenClassificationModel"]
    
    Datasets --> SaprotDatasets["SaProt Datasets"]
    Datasets --> ProtT5Datasets["ProtT5 Datasets"]
    
    WandbLoader --> |"configures"| WandbLogger["WandB Logger"]
    TrainerLoader --> |"creates"| PLTrainer["PyTorch Lightning Trainer"]
```

The module loading system centralizes component initialization and provides a standardized approach for loading different types of modules based on configuration parameters.

### Model Loading

The system dynamically loads model classes based on the specified model type in the configuration:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Config["Configuration"] --> |"model_py_path"| ModelType["Model Type Selection"]
    
    ModelType --> ModelImport["Import Specific Model Class"]
    ModelImport --> ModelInit["Initialize Model with Parameters"]
    
    ModelInit --> |"saprot/saprot_classification_model"| SCM["SaprotClassificationModel"]
    ModelInit --> |"saprot/saprot_regression_model"| SRM["SaprotRegressionModel"]
    ModelInit --> |"saprot/saprot_token_classification_model"| STCM["SaprotTokenClassificationModel"]
    ModelInit --> |"saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model"| SPCM["SaprotPairClassificationModel"]
    ModelInit --> |"saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model"| SPRM["SaprotPairRegressionModel"]
    
    ModelInit --> |"protT5/protT5_classification_model"| PCM["ProtT5ClassificationModel"]
    ModelInit --> |"protT5/protT5_regression_model"| PRM["ProtT5RegressionModel"]
    ModelInit --> |"protT5/protT5_token_classification_model"| PTCM["ProtT5TokenClassificationModel"]
```

The `my_load_model` function in the module loader handles this dynamic loading process:

```python
def my_load_model(config):
    model_config = copy.deepcopy(config)
    model_type = model_config.pop("model_py_path")

    if "kwargs" in model_config.keys():
        kwargs = model_config.pop('kwargs')
    else:
        kwargs = {}
    
    model_config.update(kwargs)

    # Import and initialize specific model class based on model_type
    if model_type == "saprot/saprot_classification_model":
      from model.saprot.saprot_classification_model import SaprotClassificationModel
      return SaprotClassificationModel(**model_config)
    
    # ... additional model types
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:15-58]()

### Dataset Loading

Similarly, datasets are loaded dynamically based on the dataset type specified in the configuration:

```python
def my_load_dataset(config):
    dataset_config = copy.deepcopy(config)
    dataset_type = dataset_config.pop("dataset_py_path")
    kwargs = dataset_config.pop('kwargs')
    dataset_config.update(kwargs)

    if dataset_type == "saprot/saprot_classification_dataset":
      from dataset.saprot.saprot_classification_dataset import SaprotClassificationDataset
      return SaprotClassificationDataset(**dataset_config)
    
    # ... additional dataset types
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:64-101]()

### Trainer and Logger Integration

The module loader also handles the initialization of PyTorch Lightning trainers and WandB integration:

```python
def load_wandb(config):
    # initialize wandb
    wandb_config = config.setting.wandb_config
    wandb_logger = WandbLogger(project=wandb_config.project, config=config,
                               name=wandb_config.name,
                               settings=wandb.Settings())
    
    return wandb_logger

def load_trainer(config):
    trainer_config = copy.deepcopy(config.Trainer)
    
    # Initialize wandb
    if trainer_config.logger:
        trainer_config.logger = load_wandb(config)
    else:
        trainer_config.logger = False
    
    # Initialize strategy
    # strategy = load_strategy(trainer_config.pop('strategy'))
    # Strategy is not used in Colab
    trainer_config.pop('strategy')
    
    return pl.Trainer(**trainer_config, callbacks=[], use_distributed_sampler=False)
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:103-187]()

## 7.2 Zero-Shot Mutation Prediction

SaprotHub provides capabilities for zero-shot mutation prediction, allowing researchers to predict the effects of protein mutations without specific training on mutation datasets.

### Conceptual Overview

Zero-shot mutation prediction enables estimating the impact of amino acid substitutions on protein function without requiring prior examples of that specific mutation. This is particularly valuable for exploring novel mutations where experimental data is unavailable.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    WildType["Wild Type Protein Sequence"] --> Encoding["Protein Encoder"]
    Mutant["Mutated Protein Sequence"] --> Encoding
    
    Encoding --> |"wild type embedding"| WildEmbed["Wild Type Embedding"]
    Encoding --> |"mutant embedding"| MutEmbed["Mutant Embedding"]
    
    WildEmbed --> Comparison["Embedding Comparison"]
    MutEmbed --> Comparison
    
    Comparison --> |"compute embedding distance"| Effect["Predicted Mutation Effect"]
    Effect --> |"stability effects"| Stability["Stability Score"]
    Effect --> |"functional effects"| Function["Functional Score"]
```

### MutationZeroShotDataset

SaprotHub implements a specialized dataset class for handling mutation data in a zero-shot prediction context:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    LMDBDataset <|-- MutationZeroShotDataset
    
    class LMDBDataset {
        +_get(index)
        +__getitem__(index)
        +__len__()
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class MutationZeroShotDataset {
        +__init__(**kwargs)
        +__getitem__(index)
        +__len__()
        +collate_fn(batch)
    }
```

The `MutationZeroShotDataset` extends the base `LMDBDataset` class to provide specialized handling for mutation data:

```python
@register_dataset
class MutationZeroShotDataset(LMDBDataset):
    """
    Dataset that deals with mutation data for zero-shot prediction
    """

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        """
        Args: **kwargs: other arguments for LMDBDataset
        """
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        data = json.loads(self._get(index))
        return data["seq"], data["mut_info"], data["fitness"]

    def __len__(self):
        return int(self._get("length"))

    def collate_fn(self, batch):
        seqs, mut_info, fitness = zip(*batch)
        
        plddt = self._get("plddt")
        if plddt is not None:
            plddt = json.loads(plddt)
        
        inputs = {"wild_type": self._get("wild_type"),
                  "seqs": seqs,
                  "mut_info": mut_info,
                  "structure_content": self._get("structure_content"),
                  "structure_type": self._get("structure_type"),
                  "plddt": plddt}

        labels = {"labels": torch.Tensor(fitness)}

        return inputs, labels
```

Sources: [saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py:1-46]()

### Data Format for Mutation Prediction

The mutation zero-shot dataset expects data in a specific format:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `seq` | Amino acid sequence of the mutated protein |
| `mut_info` | Information about the mutation (position, original amino acid, substitution) |
| `fitness` | The fitness or stability score of the mutated protein (used as ground truth) |
| `wild_type` | The reference/wild-type protein sequence |
| `structure_content` | Structural information about the protein (when available) |
| `structure_type` | Type of structure data (PDB, mmCIF, etc.) |
| `plddt` | Per-residue confidence scores (for AlphaFold structures) |

### Prediction Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input Mutation Data"] --> Dataset["MutationZeroShotDataset"]
    Dataset --> DataLoader["PyTorch DataLoader"]
    
    DataLoader --> |"batch data"| Model["Protein Language Model"]
    Model --> |"compute embeddings"| Embeddings["Protein Embeddings"]
    
    Embeddings --> |"differential analysis"| DiffAnalysis["Difference Analysis"]
    DiffAnalysis --> |"compute impact score"| Score["Mutation Impact Score"]
    
    Score --> |"interpret"| Interpretation["Interpret Results"]
```

## 7.3 Search Engine Integration

SaprotHub includes a search engine functionality that enables users to efficiently find models and datasets based on various criteria.

### Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    User["SaprotHub User"] --> |"search query"| SearchInterface["Search Interface"]
    
    SearchInterface --> ModelSearch["Model Search"]
    SearchInterface --> DatasetSearch["Dataset Search"]
    
    ModelSearch --> |"query"| HFSearch["HuggingFace Hub Search"]
    DatasetSearch --> |"query"| HFSearch
    DatasetSearch --> |"query"| LocalDB["Local Dataset Index"]
    
    HFSearch --> |"results"| ModelResults["Model Results"]
    LocalDB --> |"results"| DatasetResults["Dataset Results"]
    
    ModelResults --> ModelList["List of Available Models"]
    DatasetResults --> DatasetList["List of Available Datasets"]
    
    ModelList --> |"select"| ModelLoader["Model Loader System"]
    DatasetList --> |"select"| DatasetLoader["Dataset Loader System"]
    
    ModelLoader --> InitModel["Initialize Selected Model"]
    DatasetLoader --> InitDataset["Load Selected Dataset"]
```

### Searching for Models

The search engine allows users to find models on HuggingFace Hub using various criteria:

- Task-specific models (classification, regression, token classification)
- Specific proteins or protein families
- Models trained on structural vs. sequence data
- Performance metrics
- Publication or author information

### Dataset Search Capabilities

Users can search for available datasets:

- By protein family or function
- By task type (classification, regression)
- By data format (sequence, structure, or both)
- By size and content characteristics

### Integration with HuggingFace Hub

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SaprotHub["SaprotHub System"] --> |"search request"| HFInterface["HuggingFace Interface"]
    
    HFInterface --> |"API call"| HFHub["HuggingFace Hub"]
    HFHub --> |"search results"| HFInterface
    
    HFInterface --> |"filtered results"| SaprotHub
    SaprotHub --> |"download request"| HFInterface
    HFInterface --> |"model download"| HFHub
    
    HFHub --> |"model files"| HFInterface
    HFInterface --> |"load model"| ModuleLoader["Module Loader System"]
    ModuleLoader --> |"initialize"| Model["Model Instance"]
```

### Search Workflow Example

1. User inputs search criteria (e.g., classification models for thermostability prediction)
2. Search interface queries HuggingFace Hub and local indices
3. Results are displayed in a sorted, filterable format
4. User selects a model or dataset
5. Module loader system loads the selected model or dataset
6. The model becomes available for fine-tuning or prediction

The search engine integration significantly improves the user experience by simplifying the discovery and utilization of appropriate models and datasets for specific research needs.

# Page: Module Loading System

# Module Loading System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [saprot/utils/module_loader.py](saprot/utils/module_loader.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The Module Loading System is a core component of SaprotHub that provides dynamic, configuration-based loading of models, datasets, and training infrastructure. It enables the framework to flexibly instantiate different components based on configuration parameters rather than hard-coded implementations. This document explains how the module loading system works, its architecture, and its role in enabling the dynamic behavior of SaprotHub.

The module loading system primarily handles:
- Dynamic model instantiation
- Dataset loading
- Training configuration (including WandB logging and PyTorch Lightning trainer setup)

For information about model architecture specifics, see [Model Architecture](#3).
For information about data processing, see [Data Processing](#4).

## System Architecture Overview

The Module Loading System serves as a bridge between configuration parameters and concrete implementations of models and datasets. It translates high-level specifications into instantiated objects ready for training or inference.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Module Loading System"
        ModuleLoader["Module Loader"]
        ModelLoader["Model Loader\n(my_load_model/load_model)"]
        DatasetLoader["Dataset Loader\n(my_load_dataset/load_dataset)"]
        TrainerLoader["Trainer Loader\n(load_trainer)"]
        WandbLoader["WandB Logger\n(load_wandb)"]
        StrategyLoader["Strategy Loader\n(load_strategy)"]
    end
    
    Config["Configuration\n(model_py_path/dataset_py_path)"] --> ModuleLoader
    ModuleLoader --> ModelLoader
    ModuleLoader --> DatasetLoader
    ModuleLoader --> TrainerLoader
    
    TrainerLoader --> WandbLoader
    TrainerLoader --> StrategyLoader
    
    ModelLoader --> ModelInterface["ModelInterface.init_model()"]
    DatasetLoader --> DataInterface["DataInterface.init_dataset()"]
    
    ModelLoader --> ConcreteModels["Concrete Model Implementations\n(SaprotClassificationModel, ProtT5RegressionModel, etc.)"]
    DatasetLoader --> ConcreteDatasets["Concrete Dataset Implementations\n(SaprotRegressionDataset, ProtT5TokenClassificationDataset, etc.)"]
    
    TrainerLoader --> PyTorchTrainer["PyTorch Lightning Trainer"]
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:13-187]()

## Model Loading Subsystem

The model loading subsystem is responsible for dynamically instantiating the appropriate model class based on configuration parameters. It supports both direct loading (`my_load_model`) and interface-based loading (`load_model`).

### Direct Model Loading

The `my_load_model` function directly imports and instantiates specific model classes based on the `model_py_path` parameter:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Config["Configuration with model_py_path"] --> MyLoadModel["my_load_model()"]
    
    MyLoadModel --> ModelType{"model_py_path?"}
    
    ModelType -->|"saprot/saprot_classification_model"| SaprotCls["SaprotClassificationModel"]
    ModelType -->|"saprot/saprot_token_classification_model"| SaprotToken["SaprotTokenClassificationModel"]
    ModelType -->|"saprot/saprot_regression_model"| SaprotReg["SaprotRegressionModel"]
    ModelType -->|"saprot/saprot_pair_classification_model"| SaprotPairCls["SaprotPairClassificationModel"]
    ModelType -->|"saprot/saprot_pair_regression_model"| SaprotPairReg["SaprotPairRegressionModel"]
    ModelType -->|"protT5/protT5_classification_model"| ProtT5Cls["ProtT5ClassificationModel"]
    ModelType -->|"protT5/protT5_regression_model"| ProtT5Reg["ProtT5RegressionModel"]
    ModelType -->|"protT5/protT5_token_classification_model"| ProtT5Token["ProtT5TokenClassificationModel"]
    
    SaprotCls --> InstantiatedModel["Instantiated Model"]
    SaprotToken --> InstantiatedModel
    SaprotReg --> InstantiatedModel
    SaprotPairCls --> InstantiatedModel
    SaprotPairReg --> InstantiatedModel
    ProtT5Cls --> InstantiatedModel
    ProtT5Reg --> InstantiatedModel
    ProtT5Token --> InstantiatedModel
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:15-58]()


Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:173-187]()

## Configuration-Based Loading System

The module loading system in SaprotHub follows a configuration-based approach, where components are instantiated based on configuration dictionaries rather than direct code references. This enables several key benefits:

### Configuration Structure and Parameters

| Configuration Key | Purpose | Example Value |
|------------------|---------|---------------|
| `model_py_path`  | Identifies the model type to load | `"saprot/saprot_classification_model"` |
| `dataset_py_path` | Identifies the dataset type to load | `"saprot/saprot_regression_dataset"` |
| `kwargs` | Additional parameters for model/dataset | `{"num_labels": 3, "task": "classification"}` |
| `Trainer` | PyTorch Lightning trainer parameters | `{"logger": true, "max_epochs": 10}` |
| `setting.wandb_config` | WandB logger configuration | `{"project": "protein_classification", "name": "experiment1"}` |

### Benefits of Dynamic Loading

1. **Flexibility**: Allows switching between different model and dataset types without changing core code
2. **Extensibility**: New model and dataset types can be added by extending the conditional logic
3. **Configuration-driven**: System behavior can be changed through configuration files rather than code changes
4. **Separation of concerns**: The loading system is decoupled from the actual model and dataset implementations

## Integration with the Broader SaprotHub System

The Module Loading System plays a critical role in the SaprotHub architecture by connecting the user interface components with the underlying model and dataset implementations:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "User Interface Layer"
        ColabSaprot["ColabSaprot Interface"]
        ColabProtT5["ColabProtT5 Interface"]
        ColabProTrek["ColabProTrek Interface"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Module Loading System"
        ModuleLoader["Module Loader\n(module_loader.py)"]
        ModelLoader["Model Loader"]
        DatasetLoader["Dataset Loader"]
        TrainerLoader["Trainer Loader"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Implementation Layer"
        SaprotModels["SaProt Models\n(Classification, Regression, Token, Pair)"]
        ProtT5Models["ProtT5 Models\n(Classification, Regression, Token)"]
        Datasets["Dataset Implementations\n(LMDB-based)"]
        TrainingInfra["Training Infrastructure\n(PyTorch Lightning, WandB)"]
    end
    
    ColabSaprot --> ModuleLoader
    ColabProtT5 --> ModuleLoader
    ColabProTrek --> ModuleLoader
    
    ModuleLoader --> ModelLoader
    ModuleLoader --> DatasetLoader
    ModuleLoader --> TrainerLoader
    
    ModelLoader --> SaprotModels
    ModelLoader --> ProtT5Models
    DatasetLoader --> Datasets
    TrainerLoader --> TrainingInfra
```

Sources: [saprot/utils/module_loader.py:1-187]()

## Usage Example

When a user wants to train a new model through the SaprotHub interface, the module loading system enables this workflow:

1. User selects model type and parameters in the interface
2. Interface constructs a configuration dictionary
3. Module loading system uses that configuration to:
   - Load the appropriate model class
   - Load the appropriate dataset
   - Configure the training environment (trainer, logger)
4. Training begins with all components properly instantiated

This approach allows users to focus on the high-level task rather than implementation details, while still providing flexibility for advanced users who want to customize the components.

# Page: Zero-Shot Mutation Prediction

# Zero-Shot Mutation Prediction

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [Figure/mutational_effect_prediction/dataset/pdb.png](Figure/mutational_effect_prediction/dataset/pdb.png)
- [Figure/mutational_effect_prediction/dataset/sa.png](Figure/mutational_effect_prediction/dataset/sa.png)
- [Figure/mutational_effect_prediction/dataset/uniprot_id.png](Figure/mutational_effect_prediction/dataset/uniprot_id.png)
- [saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py](saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py)

</details>



Zero-Shot Mutation Prediction is a powerful feature in SaprotHub that enables users to predict the effects of protein mutations without requiring training data for those specific mutations. This capability leverages the general understanding of protein sequence-structure-function relationships that pre-trained protein language models have acquired during their training.

For information about more general protein mutation prediction tasks that require training on mutation datasets, see [Model Types and Prediction Tasks](#3.3).

## Overview

Zero-shot mutation prediction allows researchers to estimate how mutations will affect protein properties such as stability, function, or fitness, even for mutations that were not present in any training dataset. This is particularly valuable for protein engineering applications where experimental data for novel mutations might be limited or unavailable.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Input Data"
        WT["Wild-type Sequence"]
        MutInfo["Mutation Information"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Prediction System"
        PLM["Protein Language Model"]
        DeltaRep["Representation Difference"]
        Predict["Effect Predictor"]
    end
    
    WT --> PLM
    MutInfo --> PLM
    PLM --> DeltaRep
    DeltaRep --> Predict
    Predict --> Effect["Predicted Mutation Effect"]
```

Sources:
- saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py

## Dataset Structure for Mutation Prediction

SaprotHub implements a specialized dataset class called `MutationZeroShotDataset` to handle mutation data for zero-shot prediction tasks. This dataset inherits from the core `LMDBDataset` class and provides specific methods for working with mutation data.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class LMDBDataset {
      +__init__(kwargs)
      +_get(index)
      +__getitem__(index)
      +__len__()
      +collate_fn(batch)
    }
    
    class MutationZeroShotDataset {
      +__init__(kwargs)
      +__getitem__(index): returns seq, mut_info, fitness
      +__len__(): returns dataset length
      +collate_fn(batch): prepares data batch
    }
    
    LMDBDataset <|-- MutationZeroShotDataset
```

Each item in the dataset contains:
- The protein sequence (`seq`)
- Mutation information (`mut_info`) detailing the amino acid changes
- Fitness or functional scores (`fitness`) associated with the mutations

The dataset also maintains reference information such as:
- The wild-type sequence
- Structure content and type when available
- pLDDT (predicted local distance difference test) scores for structural confidence

Sources:
- saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py

## Technical Implementation

The `MutationZeroShotDataset` class is implemented as follows:

1. **Initialization**: Inherits from `LMDBDataset` and uses its infrastructure for storing and retrieving data
2. **Item Retrieval**: The `__getitem__` method returns a tuple of (`seq`, `mut_info`, `fitness`) for each item
3. **Batch Preparation**: The `collate_fn` method prepares batches for model processing, aggregating key information:
   - Wild-type sequence
   - Mutant sequences
   - Mutation information
   - Structure data (when available)
   - pLDDT scores (when available)

This data organization enables the model to compare wild-type and mutant sequences effectively for prediction.

```python
# Key functionality from MutationZeroShotDataset
def __getitem__(self, index):
    data = json.loads(self._get(index))
    return data["seq"], data["mut_info"], data["fitness"]

def collate_fn(self, batch):
    seqs, mut_info, fitness = zip(*batch)
    
    # Get structural data if available
    plddt = self._get("plddt")
    if plddt is not None:
        plddt = json.loads(plddt)
    
    # Create inputs dictionary with all context
    inputs = {"wild_type": self._get("wild_type"),
              "seqs": seqs,
              "mut_info": mut_info,
              "structure_content": self._get("structure_content"),
              "structure_type": self._get("structure_type"),
              "plddt": plddt}

    # Convert fitness values to tensor
    labels = {"labels": torch.Tensor(fitness)}

    return inputs, labels
```

Sources:
- saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py

## Data Flow for Mutation Prediction

The following diagram illustrates how data flows through the SaprotHub system for zero-shot mutation prediction:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "User Interface"

        Results["Prediction Results"]

    MutZeroShotDS --> LMDB
    LMDB --> DataLoader

    SaprotRegModel --> Embedder
    Embedder --> RegressionHead["Regression Head"]
    RegressionHead --> Results
```

Sources:
- saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py

## Prediction Mechanism

The zero-shot mutation prediction works through the following process:

1. **Embedding Generation**: The model generates embeddings for both wild-type and mutant sequences
2. **Representation Comparison**: The system analyzes differences between these embeddings
3. **Effect Prediction**: Based on the embedding differences, the model predicts the mutation's effect on protein properties

When structural information is available, it can significantly enhance prediction accuracy by providing context about the 3D environment of the mutation site.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input"
        WT["Wild-type Sequence"]
        Mut["Mutation A15G"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        Embed["Protein Embedding"]
        Compare["Embedding Comparison"]
        Predict["Effect Prediction"]
    end
    
    WT --> Embed
    Mut --> Embed
    Embed --> Compare
    Compare --> Predict
    
    Structure["Structure Information"] --> Embed
    
    Predict --> Effect["Predicted Fitness Change"]
```

## Integrating Structure Information

SaprotHub can enhance mutation prediction by incorporating structural information when available:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SeqInput["Sequence Input"] --> SeqEmbed["Sequence Embedding"]
    StructInput["Structure Input"] --> StructEmbed["Structure-Aware Embedding"]
    
    SeqEmbed --> CombinedEmbed["Combined Representation"]
    StructEmbed --> CombinedEmbed
    
    CombinedEmbed --> MutEffect["Mutation Effect Prediction"]
    
    subgraph "Structure Sources"
        PDB["PDB Structure"]
        AlphaFold["AlphaFold Prediction"]
        ESMFold["ESMFold Prediction"]
    end
    
    PDB --> StructInput
    AlphaFold --> StructInput
    ESMFold --> StructInput
```

Sources:
- saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py

## How to Use Zero-Shot Mutation Prediction

To use the zero-shot mutation prediction capability in SaprotHub:

1. **Prepare your mutation data**: Format your data with the wild-type sequence and the desired mutations.
2. **Create a dataset**: Use the `MutationZeroShotDataset` class to load your mutation data.
3. **Run prediction**: Use a pre-trained protein language model to predict the effects of the mutations.

### Example Usage Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Dataset as MutationZeroShotDataset
    participant Model as SaprotRegressionModel
    
    User->>Dataset: Create dataset with mutation data
    User->>Model: Load pre-trained model
    User->>Model: Request prediction
    
    Model->>Dataset: Get batch of data
    Dataset->>Model: Return sequences and context
    
    Model->>Model: Generate embeddings
    Model->>Model: Predict mutation effects
    
    Model->>User: Return predictions
```

## Applications

Zero-shot mutation prediction is particularly valuable for:

| Application | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| Protein Engineering | Rapidly screening potential mutations for desired properties without experimental testing |
| Variant Effect Prediction | Assessing the impact of genetic variants on protein function |
| Antibody Design | Optimizing antibody sequences for improved binding or specificity |
| Enzyme Optimization | Identifying mutations that might enhance enzyme activity or stability |
| Drug Resistance | Predicting mutations that might confer resistance to drugs or treatments |

## Limitations and Considerations

While zero-shot mutation prediction is powerful, users should be aware of its limitations:

- Predictions are based on patterns learned from pre-training data and may not capture all protein-specific nuances
- Accuracy varies depending on protein family representation in the pre-training data
- Structural context significantly affects prediction accuracy, especially for mutations in functional sites
- Complex epistatic interactions between multiple mutations may not be fully captured
- Performance may vary depending on the distance between the query protein and proteins in the training data

## References and Related Pages

- For more information on the general model architecture, see [Model Architecture](#3)
- For details on dataset handling, see [Datasets and Data Formats](#4.1)
- For LMDB dataset construction, see [LMDB Dataset Construction](#4.2)
- For protein structure handling, see [Protein Structure Handling](#4.3)

Sources:
- saprot/dataset/mutation_zeroshot_dataset.py

# Page: Search Engine Integration

# Search Engine Integration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [search_engine/app.py](search_engine/app.py)
- [search_engine/loop_retrieve_cards.py](search_engine/loop_retrieve_cards.py)
- [search_engine/utils.py](search_engine/utils.py)

</details>



The Search Engine Integration in SaprotHub provides a powerful interface for discovering and exploring available protein language models and datasets. This system allows researchers to efficiently search through models and datasets hosted on the HuggingFace Hub by the SaprotHub team, making it easier to find appropriate resources for specific protein analysis tasks.

## 1. Overview

The search engine offers a simple yet effective way to search across model and dataset repositories using keywords. It retrieves information from HuggingFace, highlighting matches in both repository names and their README documentation, providing an organized view of available resources.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "User Interface"
        UI["Search Interface"]
        Query["Search Query"]
        Results["Search Results"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Search Logic"
        Matcher["Pattern Matching"]
        Highlighter["Text Highlighting"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Sources"
        HF["HuggingFace API"]
        Models["SaprotHub Models"]
        Datasets["SaprotHub Datasets"]
        READMEs["Repository READMEs"]
    end
    
    UI --> Query
    Query --> Matcher
    Matcher --> Results
    Highlighter --> Results
    
    HF --> Models
    HF --> Datasets
    HF --> READMEs
    
    Models --> Matcher
    Datasets --> Matcher
    READMEs --> Matcher
    
    Matcher --> Highlighter
```

Sources: [search_engine/app.py:1-84](), [search_engine/utils.py:1-89](), [search_engine/loop_retrieve_cards.py:1-57]()

## 2. Architecture Components

The search engine consists of three main components:

1. **User Interface** - A Gradio-based web interface for submitting search queries
2. **Data Retrieval** - Background processes that fetch model and dataset information
3. **Search Logic** - Functions that match query terms and format results

### 2.1 Component Interaction

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant "Gradio Interface" as Gradio
    participant "Search Logic" as Search
    participant "Data Cache" as Cache
    participant "HuggingFace API" as HF
    
    Note over Cache, HF: Background Thread
    HF->>Cache: Fetch models
    HF->>Cache: Fetch datasets
    HF->>Cache: Fetch READMEs
    
    User->>Gradio: Enter search term
    Gradio->>Search: Pass query
    Search->>Cache: Get models
    Search->>Cache: Get datasets
    Search->>Cache: Get README content
    Search->>Search: Match query in content
    Search->>Gradio: Return formatted results
    Gradio->>User: Display results
```

Sources: [search_engine/app.py:67-83](), [search_engine/loop_retrieve_cards.py:29-56]()

## 3. Implementation Details

### 3.1 Data Retrieval System

The search engine uses a background thread to continuously update its cache of models, datasets, and README files from HuggingFace. This ensures that the search results always reflect the most recent repositories without requiring manual updates.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Background Thread"
        FetchModels["fetch_models()"]
        FetchDatasets["fetch_datasets()"]
        FetchREADMEs["fetch_readme()"]
        UpdateCache["Update Global Cache"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cache"
        ModelsCache["models"]
        DatasetsCache["datasets"]
        ReadmeCache["readme_dict"]
    end
    
    FetchModels --> FetchREADMEs
    FetchDatasets --> FetchREADMEs
    FetchREADMEs --> UpdateCache
    
    UpdateCache --> ModelsCache
    UpdateCache --> DatasetsCache
    UpdateCache --> ReadmeCache
    
    ModelsCache -.-> |"get_models()"| Search["Search Function"]
    DatasetsCache -.-> |"get_datasets()"| Search
    ReadmeCache -.-> |"get_readme_dict()"| Search
```

Sources: [search_engine/loop_retrieve_cards.py:1-57](), [search_engine/utils.py:5-63]()

### 3.2 Search Functionality

The search algorithm works by:

1. Taking a user input query string
2. Searching for this string in model/dataset names and README contents
3. Highlighting matches using HTML span elements
4. Organizing results by type (models and datasets)
5. Providing direct links to the HuggingFace repositories

The search is case-insensitive and filters out matches that only appear in HTML comments.

Table: Core Search Functions

| Function | Purpose | File Location |
|----------|---------|---------------|
| `match_card()` | Searches for query in a specific card and formats the result | [search_engine/app.py:13-48]() |
| `show_card_info()` | Processes all models and datasets for matches | [search_engine/app.py:51-65]() |
| `set_text_bg_color()` | Highlights matched text in search results | [search_engine/utils.py:65-88]() |

Sources: [search_engine/app.py:13-65](), [search_engine/utils.py:65-88]()

### 3.3 User Interface

The search interface is built using Gradio, a Python library for creating customizable web interfaces. The UI consists of:

1. A simple text input box for entering search terms
2. A results area that updates automatically as you type
3. Sections for models and datasets, each with highlighted matches

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GradioInterface {
        +search_box: Textbox
        +search_hint: Markdown
        +items: Markdown
        +change() Search for matches
    }
    
    class SearchFunctions {
        +show_card_info(input: str)
        +match_card(input: str, card_id: str, card_type: str)
    }
    
    class DataProviders {
        +get_models()
        +get_datasets()
        +get_readme_dict()
    }
    
    GradioInterface --> SearchFunctions: Uses
    SearchFunctions --> DataProviders: Retrieves data from
```

Sources: [search_engine/app.py:68-83]()

## 4. API Interactions with HuggingFace

The search engine interacts with the HuggingFace API to retrieve model and dataset information. The system uses HuggingFace Mirror (`hf-mirror.com`) as the API endpoint, which may provide better performance depending on geographic location.

### 4.1 HuggingFace API Requests

Table: HuggingFace API Endpoints Used

| Function | Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `fetch_models()` | `https://hf-mirror.com/api/models?author=SaProtHub` | Retrieves all models by SaprotHub |
| `fetch_datasets()` | `https://hf-mirror.com/api/datasets?author=SaProtHub` | Retrieves all datasets by SaprotHub |
| `fetch_readme()` (models) | `https://hf-mirror.com/{card_id}/raw/main/README.md` | Gets README for a specific model |
| `fetch_readme()` (datasets) | `https://hf-mirror.com/datasets/{card_id}/raw/main/README.md` | Gets README for a specific dataset |

Sources: [search_engine/utils.py:5-63]()

## 5. Usage

### 5.1 Accessing the Search Engine

The search engine can be started by running the app.py file, which launches a Gradio server:

```bash
python search_engine/app.py
```

This starts a web server on `0.0.0.0` which makes the search interface accessible from a web browser.

### 5.2 Performing Searches

1. Enter a keyword in the search box
2. Results will automatically update as you type
3. Matches are highlighted in yellow
4. Click on model/dataset names to visit their HuggingFace repositories

### 5.3 Search Result Structure

Search results are organized into two main sections:

1. **Models** - Matching protein language models (e.g., SaProt-based models for specific tasks)
2. **Datasets** - Matching protein datasets used for training or evaluation

Each result includes:
- Repository name with link to HuggingFace
- Highlighted snippets from README that match your search term

Sources: [search_engine/app.py:51-65]()

## 6. Integration with SaprotHub

The search engine serves as a discovery tool within the broader SaprotHub ecosystem, helping researchers find appropriate pre-trained models and datasets for their specific protein analysis tasks. It complements the model training and fine-tuning capabilities of SaprotHub by making it easy to find existing resources before deciding to train new models.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "SaprotHub Ecosystem"
        Interface["ColabSaprot Interface"]
        Training["Model Training"]
        Deployment["Model Deployment"]
        SearchEngine["Search Engine"]
    end
    
    User["Researcher"] --> SearchEngine
    SearchEngine --> |"Find models"| HF["HuggingFace"]
    HF --> |"Select model"| Interface
    Interface --> Training
    Training --> Deployment
    
    SearchEngine -.-> |"Informs"| Training
```

The search engine integration helps researchers efficiently navigate the growing collection of protein language models and datasets within the SaprotHub project, enabling them to build upon existing work and focus their research efforts.
